chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #34, NEMT & Medical Courier Dispatch Arbitrage, ranks #08 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its leverage disappears when operators confuse authorized trips with collectible claims or gross billings with retained revenue. This chapter examines nine mapped plays: standing-order NEMT, discharge transport, wheelchair service, workers'-comp transport, rural mileage, scheduled specimen routes, STAT pickups, overflow dispatch, and adjacent DME/telehealth acquisition. These are chapter-level operating mappings, not nine supplied catalog identifiers. Canonical annual owner profits are $30,000 Conservative, $166,500 Base, and $384,000 Scaled. The controls target evidence defects, payment float, worker classification, specimen failures, and referral-payment exposure. The question's 80% framing is not a measured failure rate; the useful deliverable is an auditable stop-loss system.

sections.heading: 1. Separate Collectible Dispatch Contribution from Attractive Trip Volume
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is buying volume with money that belongs to drivers. Formula v2.0 assigns 55% of gross contracted billings to driver settlements and 45% to retained dispatch contribution. Conservative billings of $250,000 therefore produce $137,500 of settlements and $112,500 retained; subtract $82,500 of remaining modeled costs to reach $30,000 owner profit. Base billings of $925,000 produce $508,750 of settlements and $416,250 retained; $249,750 of remaining costs leave $166,500. Scaled billings of $1,600,000 produce $880,000 of settlements and $720,000 retained; $336,000 of remaining costs leave $384,000. These are scenario identities, not a forecast that every route earns the same spread. Under the supplied ASC 606 net presentation, retained revenue is the operator's revenue basis; gross billings measure contract throughput. Actual principal-versus-agent presentation requires contract-specific analysis. Client healthcare charges, specimen testing receipts, and vehicle asset values are neither dispatch revenue nor margin. The advertised monthly operating-expense range cannot silently replace the complete annual cost residuals above. Maintain separate settlement, overhead, exception-cost, and owner-profit ledgers so a cheap-looking route cannot hide its support burden. Count founders performing dispatch inside the stated team capacity rather than presenting their labor as unlimited.

The second trap is treating Net-45 as forty-five days after pickup rather than forty-five days after a clean, accepted invoice. At Base throughput, $508,750 divided by 365 means approximately $1,394 of daily driver obligations. A forty-five-day settlement funding interval consumes about $62,723 before overhead. Including the $249,750 remaining annual cost base lifts that simple cash bridge to approximately $93,514, assuming level activity, immediate cost payment, and no receipts during the interval. Actual weekly settlements change timing, not the underlying mismatch. That illustrative requirement exceeds the $65,000 upper startup-capital figure, so ramp size, payment terms, and committed liquidity must be solved before accepting Base volume. Neither borrowing capacity nor uncollected invoices count as available cash until actually accessible. A fifteen-day payer delay adds roughly $20,908 of driver funding alone. Track pickup-to-submission, submission-to-acceptance, and acceptance-to-cash separately; otherwise clerical delays masquerade as payer behavior. Use a rolling thirteen-week cash forecast and exclude disputed receivables from available coverage. Pause incremental commitments when unrestricted cash plus drawable facilities cannot fund the next two settlement cycles and essential overhead. This is a proposed internal threshold, not a payer rule. Negotiate smaller launch batches rather than withholding money already earned by drivers.

The third trap is quoting only loaded miles while paying for empty repositioning, waiting, cancellation, and rescue capacity. For the standing-order NEMT mapping, twenty completed legs at $40 generate $800 gross and $360 retained at the canonical share. If two completed legs become wholly uncollectible after driver payment, retained contribution falls to $280, not $324, because the original $440 settlement remains due. For discharge transport, six $65 trips yield $390 gross and $175.50 retained; a documented $60 rescue expense reduces contribution to $115.50 before overhead. Wheelchair service illustrates equipment mismatch: four $90 legs yield $360 gross and $162 retained, but one $90 refund plus a $50 replacement vehicle consumes $140. These are illustrative unit tests, not additions to the canonical annual cases. Require separate written rates for attendant needs, stairs, wait time, after-hours work, and cancellations where the contract permits payment. Never bill a wheelchair code merely because a vehicle can carry a chair. Fall back to verified ambulatory-only work when securement capability, driver training, or accessible backup capacity fails. Measure realized contribution per occupied vehicle-hour and total route-hour; a high ticket can still lose money across the driver's full assignment.

sections.heading: 2. Make Every Paid Trip Survive an Authorization and Evidence Audit
paragraphs: The fourth trap is assuming an appointment, a facility request, and a payable transport authorization are interchangeable. Medicaid transportation arrangements operate through state requirements and broker contracts; 42 CFR 431.53 establishes the transportation assurance, not a universal rate or invoice format. Confirm member eligibility for the service date, authorization scope, transport mode, pickup and destination, permitted escort, and provider enrollment requirements before assignment. A standing order can expire while dialysis appointments continue. A facility employee cannot necessarily authorize a higher mode or extra mileage. Workers'-comp transport is another chapter mapping: ten $70 legs produce $700 gross and $315 retained, but three unsupported $70 legs erase $210 when settlements remain payable. Its fallback is a written adjuster or authorized administrator instruction with claim-specific service limits, not submitting the same transport to Medicaid. Rural mileage is the fifth dispatch mapping: one $150 trip yields $67.50 retained; twenty unpriced miles at an illustrative $0.80 incremental operating cost consume $16. Route maps support distance review but do not override contracted mileage rules. Stop billing disputed mileage, retain the original route evidence, and obtain written clarification before expanding a geographically expensive assignment.

The fifth and sixth traps are manufacturing proof after service and mistaking electronic acceptance for payment approval. RouteGenie or MediRoutes can support dispatch and location records where configured, but software does not establish that the correct rider boarded, the authorized service occurred, or the payer accepts a particular signature method. Link dispatch identifier, driver identity, vehicle, timestamps, location events, rider acknowledgement or permitted exception, and authorization reference. Test device clock drift and offline synchronization; keep original event times distinct from upload times. An 837P workflow applies only where the payer requires professional claims; some transport brokers instead require portals, files, or proprietary invoices. Where used, a 999 or 277CA acknowledgement does not establish final payment. Reconcile adjudication and remittance, including applicable 835 adjustments, against the exact service line. Never copy signatures, fabricate GPS events, split a single trip into fictitious legs, share credentials, or resubmit paid claims under changed identifiers. Those shortcuts create evidence of intentional misrepresentation and can cause termination, recoupment, exclusion proceedings, or other liability. Correct genuine errors through the payer's documented replacement or adjustment process, preserving the original and the reason for every change. Restrict retrospective edits to named staff with recorded authority and an immutable change history.

The seventh trap is monitoring denials only after cash falls. Build a daily exception queue that distinguishes missing evidence, eligibility mismatch, duplicate transmission, authorization exhaustion, and rate variance. Proposed launch thresholds are zero invented records, zero expired credentials dispatched, same-day review of every missing completion record, and investigation when first-pass rejection exceeds 2% over the latest fifty submitted lines. Small samples require case review rather than confident statistical claims. Track rejected dollars as well as counts; one expensive wheelchair trip can outweigh several routine legs. Reconcile contracted allowed amount to actual payment before attributing every shortfall to a denial. A $3 processing deduction on one thousand trips costs $3,000 even when every claim is accepted. Contract offsets, audit lookbacks, appeal deadlines, and recovery rights belong in a payer-specific register. When an overpayment is identified, preserve evidence and apply the applicable reporting and return requirements, including 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7k(d) where relevant; contract dispute procedures do not erase statutory duties. A notice of network suspension triggers a stop on new affected assignments and coordinated continuity for existing patients. Never attempt reinstatement through another identity or replacement entity designed to conceal the sanctioned operation.

sections.heading: 3. Treat Specimen Integrity, Workforce Design, and Data Access as Loss Multipliers
paragraphs: The eighth trap is calling every medical package a routine parcel. Scheduled specimen routes and STAT pickups are separate chapter mappings because their exception economics differ. Twelve scheduled stops at $25 produce $300 gross and $135 retained at the canonical share. A $180 recollection expense would make that run negative $45 before overhead if allocated entirely to the operator under its contract. Six $80 STAT jobs produce $480 gross and $216 retained; one $250 emergency rescue leaves negative $34. Both examples require written responsibility allocation, not an assumption that the courier owes every clinical downstream loss. Require the laboratory to define collection, stability, temperature, packaging, accession, and rejection criteria. Barcode handoffs must link package identity, seal condition, custody event, and receiving acknowledgement without exposing unnecessary patient details. CLIA laboratory requirements under 42 CFR 493.1242 inform the lab's specimen procedures; they do not make an ordinary dispatch business a certified laboratory. For applicable Category B infectious substances, use 49 CFR 173.199 packaging requirements and role-appropriate instruction. UN3373 is not a blanket label for every specimen. Classification, dry ice, and air movement can introduce different requirements that must be resolved before accepting the shipment.

The ninth trap is selling a STAT promise without a clock model or qualified backup. Record request received, ready-for-pickup confirmation, assignment, arrival, custody transfer, destination arrival, and laboratory acceptance as distinct events. A driver arriving on time does not cure a specimen collected too early for the available stability window. Set dispatch alerts from the actual laboratory-defined limit: escalate when predicted acceptance would leave less than the agreed contingency buffer, rather than using a universal sixty-minute target. Quarantine temperature excursions for laboratory disposition; the dispatcher must not improvise specimen acceptability. Record logger identity, calibration status where required, packaging condition, and custody breaks. OSHA's bloodborne-pathogens standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030, applies to covered employees with occupational exposure; its exposure-control, training, protective-equipment, and post-exposure provisions cannot be replaced with a driver waiver. Evaluate each employer's duties rather than assuming contractor labels remove exposure obligations. The safe fallback is a qualified backup courier, a laboratory-directed recollection, or refusal before custody transfer when packaging is deficient. Never conceal a late delivery by changing a scan time. Track rejected specimens per thousand packages and investigate every custody loss, even when the laboratory initially absorbs the replacement cost.

The tenth and eleventh traps are treating owner-operator agreements as automatic worker classification and assuming a signed BAA authorizes every data flow. Evaluate actual scheduling control, equipment ownership, opportunity for profit or loss, substitution rights, economic dependence, and applicable state tests. California Labor Code section 2775 supplies an ABC framework subject to statutory exceptions; a business-to-business arrangement is not an automatic escape. Federal wage, tax, and state unemployment standards can differ. Budget employee conversion or use a genuine qualified carrier relationship when the operating facts do not support independent contracting. The eighth dispatch mapping, overflow brokerage, illustrates the tradeoff: ten $60 jobs yield $600 gross and $270 retained at the canonical share, but a $120 qualified-carrier premium leaves $150. Verify subcontracting permission, insurance scope, credential responsibility, and service evidence before assigning overflow. For privacy, distinguish a narrow transport-only conduit role from dispatch services that maintain or process protected health information. Execute required BAAs under 45 CFR 164.504(e), restrict access by role, and assess relevant subcontractors. Do not send rider diagnoses through personal messaging or advertising pixels. Revoke departed staff immediately and investigate cross-account access as a security incident, not merely a scheduling inconvenience.

sections.heading: 4. Reject Referral Schemes and Install a Portfolio-Level Stop-Loss
paragraphs: The ninth chapter mapping is the adjacent catalog play out_of_network_dme_telehealth_billing_arbitrage, not a transport revenue stream. Its supplied acquisition range is $85–$220 per patient, with $900–$3,500+ reimbursement and $70–$220 hardware cost. At $900 reimbursement, $220 acquisition, and $220 hardware, the arithmetic leaves $460 before clinician, fulfillment, billing, support, refunds, and other costs. At $3,500, $85, and $70, the same incomplete spread is $3,345. Neither figure is MSO revenue, a dispatch fee, or proof of collectibility. A twenty-patient campaign at $220 acquisition spends $4,400 before any service is reimbursed. If four $900 claims fail after fulfillment, expected gross collections fall $3,600 while acquisition and hardware expenditures remain. Keep this experiment outside the NEMT scorecard and outside patient trip records. The transport operator must not turn access to riders into a covert acquisition channel, sell appointment lists, or imply that a ride depends on purchasing equipment. Independent clinical evaluation, documented medical necessity, applicable coverage criteria, and supplier enrollment determine whether a claim can proceed. Paid-social symptom funnels cannot substitute for that clinical work or manufacture an order through prechecked questionnaire answers.

The twelfth trap is accepting a percentage of reimbursed healthcare claims because somebody labels the agreement an MSO retainer. For federal healthcare program business, 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b) addresses remuneration intended to induce or reward covered referrals or business. The personal-services safe harbor in 42 CFR 1001.952(d) contains specific conditions; fair-market-value wording alone does not satisfy them. The fallback is a properly structured written services arrangement with defined deliverables, documented fair market value, compensation methodology set in advance, and no prohibited volume-or-value linkage, with all applicable conditions assessed. For illustration, a $3,000 monthly software and administrative retainer produces $36,000 annual MSO billings, not the suppliers' reimbursement totals. That hypothetical retainer does not alter any canonical transport scenario. Prioritizing commercial payers and medically appropriate recurring CGM resupply does not remove state referral, fee-splitting, privacy, or payer-contract restrictions. Use independent third-party clinical chart review and keep advertising decisions separate from prescribing judgment. Reject arrangements involving purchased signatures, diagnosis coaching, concealed referral payments, or routine coding upgrades unsupported by actual service. A failed review means stop the affected acquisition channel and resolve existing patients' service continuity, not rotate domains or create replacement advertising accounts to escape enforcement.

The final trap is allowing a successful week to raise every exposure limit. Operate one dashboard across the nine chapter mappings, with separate ledgers for transport, specimens, and any adjacent MSO activity. Monitor contribution after settlements, claim defects, cash runway, payer concentration, overdue credentials, missed service windows, specimen rejection, and privacy incidents. Proposed intervention thresholds include investigating a payer above 35% of collected revenue, reviewing retained share below 42% against the canonical 45%, and freezing incremental assignments when two settlement cycles lack funding. These are management settings to calibrate against contract mix, not externally prescribed standards. At Base billings, one percentage point of gross leakage costs $9,250 annually; three points cost $27,750, reducing $166,500 owner profit to $138,750 if other costs remain unchanged. A 5% uncollectible share of Base billings costs $46,250 when drivers have already been paid and no recovery offsets exist. That is a sensitivity, not a replacement scorecard. Assign every red indicator an owner, deadline, and resumption test. Preserve records, protect patients and specimens, notify contractual counterparties when required, and stop only the affected workflow unless the failure is systemic. Growth resumes after evidence demonstrates control, not after a salesperson promises better customers.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in nemt & medical courier dispatch arbitrage, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (2–5 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Mine Medicaid Standing Orders, CLIA Laboratory Footprints, Workers' Compensation Networks, and STAT Coverage Gaps into Verified Route Contracts
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #34, NEMT & Medical Courier Dispatch Arbitrage, ranks #08 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps nine operator plays: Medicaid standing orders, dialysis corridors, discharge overflow, workers' compensation appointments, laboratory milk runs, STAT backups, rural specimen consolidation, owner-operator capacity matching, and the separately authorized WOTC/research-credit documentation engine. Build demand from public facility records and purchasing signals, qualify actual routing authority, then sell a bounded paid pilot. Canonical annual owner profits are $30,000 Conservative, $166,500 Base, and $384,000 Scaled. Gross contract billings are not retained dispatch revenue: the model retains 45% after driver settlements. A measured outreach system targets three to ten contracted wins within two to five months without buying vehicles or confusing referrals with orders.

sections.heading: 1. Mine purchasing signals, not patient identities
paragraphs: Start with one service polygon defined by drive time, receiving hours, and backup coverage, not an entire state. Build a 120-account research universe from state Medicaid transportation manuals, broker provider-network pages, public procurement portals, CMS Care Compare dialysis listings, and CMS CLIA laboratory records. Record the facility address, public purchasing contact, procurement vehicle, service window, source URL, and retrieval date. A CLIA certificate identifies a laboratory footprint; it does not reveal shipment volume, purchasing authority, or specimen classification. A dialysis station count indicates potential recurrence, not a sellable trip entitlement. Read county purchasing minutes for expiring transport contracts, hospital expansion announcements for discharge pressure, and laboratory job postings for evening accessioning shifts. Cross-check each signal by calling an administrative contact and asking who purchases transportation for that specific population. Keep patient names, diagnoses, and appointment rosters out of prospecting systems. Store only organization-level research in HubSpot or Airtable until an executed agreement and necessary access controls support operational data exchange. An attractive map becomes a lead only when a buyer confirms an unresolved service requirement, a purchasing route, and a decision date.

The first four chapter plays target recurring passenger demand. Play one, Medicaid standing orders, begins with the contracted broker's network team: facility enthusiasm alone cannot authorize reimbursable trips. An illustrative 60 authorized one-way legs weekly at $42 produces $2,520 billings and $1,134 retained contribution at 45%, before overhead. Play two, dialysis corridors, packages compatible treatment windows: 36 weekly legs at $48 yield $1,728 and $777.60 respectively. Never promise pooling when mobility needs, benefit rules, or discharge timing make it unsuitable. Play three, hospital discharge overflow, prices scarce evening coverage: 12 completed legs at $85 yield $1,020 billings and $459 retained contribution. Play four, workers' compensation appointments, approaches the authorized adjuster or transportation network: 20 approved legs at $65 yield $1,300 and $585. These are independent quoting examples, not additions to the canonical annual scenarios. Confirm whether waiting, empty repositioning, tolls, escorts, and cancellations are separately payable. If authorizations are unreliable, offer a buyer-funded limited coverage block with explicit payment responsibility, or decline the route. Do not transfer unpaid authorized-service risk to the passenger through improvised charges or represent a facility referral as payer approval.

The next four plays pursue specimens and usable capacity. Play five, laboratory milk runs, joins collection sites with compatible accession cutoffs: ten weekly route runs at $140 produce $1,400 billings and $630 retained contribution. Play six, STAT backup coverage, sells a defined response envelope: eight completed dispatches at $95 generate $760 and $342, excluding any separately negotiated availability fee. Play seven, rural specimen consolidation, needs a real receiving destination and validated transport conditions: six runs at $180 generate $1,080 and $486. Play eight, owner-operator capacity matching, fills verified service gaps rather than reselling an unapproved subcontract: 15 authorized legs at $50 generate $750 and $337.50. For every example, 55% driver settlement is a screening assumption, not a promise that every lane supports that split. Measure loaded time, empty miles, parking, cleaning, packaging handling, and return obligations before quoting. If specimen stability conflicts with consolidation, revert to dedicated transport. If a broker prohibits subcontracting, pursue direct credentialing or reject the assignment. If backup capacity disappears, reduce the offered geography instead of selling a response window that dispatch cannot deliver. The ninth, adjacent employer-service play appears separately in the conversion economics.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify authority, route contribution, and payment float before quoting
paragraphs: Use a 100-point qualification score before spending time on a custom proposal. Award 20 points for verified purchasing and assignment authority, 20 for recurring addressable volume, 20 for measured route contribution, 15 for acceptable collection terms, 15 for credentialed primary and backup capacity, and 10 for a documented buying event. Require at least 75 points for a proposal, while treating absent trip authority, unsafe handling, and prohibited subcontracting as disqualifiers regardless of score. Full volume points require a buyer-confirmed aggregate schedule, not a facility census. Full contribution points require a driver quote for the complete route and a dispatch cost estimate. Full collection points require invoice acceptance rules, dispute ownership, and a credible payer. Ask who signs, who issues the order, who accepts proof of service, and who releases payment; these can be four different organizations. Record the answer to each question in separate CRM fields. Avoid calling the deal qualified because a case manager likes the concept. If the score is below threshold, specify the missing evidence and a next review date. An unresolved credentialing dependency belongs in nurture, not the committed sales forecast.

Translate the canonical scorecard into a purchasing filter. Conservative gross billings of $250,000 less $137,500 driver settlements leave $112,500 retained revenue; $82,500 of remaining operating costs leave $30,000 owner profit. Base billings of $925,000 less $508,750 settlements leave $416,250 retained revenue; $249,750 remaining costs leave $166,500 profit. Scaled billings of $1,600,000 less $880,000 settlements leave $720,000 retained revenue; $336,000 remaining costs leave $384,000 profit. Thus gross-billings margins are 12%, 18.0%, and 24%, while retained margins are 26.67%, 40.0%, and 53.33%. Preserve the supplied 2 FT + 2 C, 2 FT + 2 C, and 3 FT + 3 C staffing assumptions. Do not reinterpret those headcounts as a universal fleet-capacity limit; validate actual driver availability against each schedule. The model uses retained dispatch revenue as its net presentation; actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment depends on the contracts and control of the promised service. Keep gross billings, driver settlements, retained contribution, and owner profit in distinct ledger fields. Reject proposals that substitute underlying medical charges or workers' compensation claim values for transport revenue. Route contribution is not owner profit.

Payment float can eliminate a superficially attractive deal. At the Base case, $508,750 annual driver settlements equal approximately $1,393.84 daily using 365 days. A 45-day interval between paying drivers and collecting accepted invoices ties up approximately $62,723 before overhead, disputes, or reserve cash. Weekly driver terms may shorten that interval, while rejected invoices can lengthen it; model actual dates rather than assuming Net-45 means exactly 45 days from pickup. This exposure nearly consumes the $65,000 upper startup-capital case, making an immediate Base-scale launch unsuitable without additional liquidity or staged volume. The supplied $3,500–$18,000 monthly opex range is a planning indicator, not the complete residual cost bridge: Base remaining costs average $20,812.50 monthly. Budget every residual category explicitly rather than forcing that total into the narrower range. Start with one bounded route, invoice promptly, and reconcile paid versus accepted service before expanding. Use 837P EDI only where the payer actually requires that transaction; other buyers use broker portals or ordinary invoices. RouteGenie or MediRoutes GPS evidence can support service verification, but neither replaces authorization, required signatures, or the payer's specified trip record.

sections.heading: 3. Run a measurable outbound cadence and convert evidence into paid pilots
paragraphs: Build outreach around one observed constraint, one credible capacity statement, and one small next step. A laboratory email can read: your public hours show collection through 18:00; we are evaluating a dedicated 18:15 pickup to your receiving laboratory, subject to your transport requirements; who owns that route? A broker email instead names the specific county, vehicle class, and verified coverage window. Do not claim network approval before it exists. On day one send a short individual email; on day three call the published business number; on day six send a one-page coverage map; on day ten offer a route review; on day fifteen close the loop and ask permission for a later check-in. Use accurate sender details, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out for commercial email under 15 U.S.C. 7704. Avoid unsolicited automated texts or prerecorded calls; screen calling methods against 47 U.S.C. 227 and applicable state rules. Log objections and suppress opt-outs across all campaigns. Public contact details are a starting point for relevant outreach, not permission to flood every employee at the same institution.

Treat conversion benchmarks as planning hypotheses, not industry averages. For one 120-account cohort, target 84 verified purchasing contacts, 42 substantive conversations, 21 qualified route assessments, 12 written proposals, six paid pilots, and three signed recurring assignments. The successive conversions are 70%, 50%, 50%, approximately 57%, 50%, and 50%; the overall win rate is 2.5%. A stretch cohort of 200 researched accounts can yield 140 contacts, 70 conversations, 35 assessments, 20 proposals, 14 pilots, and ten wins, implying 5% overall conversion and materially stronger pilot performance. Keep these funnels separate rather than averaging incompatible assumptions. Assign one person research and contracting ownership and another dispatch feasibility ownership; batch approximately ten new accounts per working day during the research phase. Use weeks one through three for mapping, weeks three through eight for conversations and credentialing, and weeks eight through twenty for pilots and recurring awards. Existing network access may compress this schedule; new enrollment can extend it beyond five months. Review losses weekly by authority, price, timing, capacity, or payment terms. Fix the largest measured bottleneck before increasing outreach volume or buying another contact list.

Design inbound material to answer the questions a real buyer asks before requesting coverage. Publish separate pages for wheelchair-capable NEMT coverage, laboratory scheduled routes, and STAT backup, using only capabilities actually supported by the operator network. Show service geography, staffed dispatch hours, vehicle or handling limitations, and a clear organizational inquiry form. Do not collect patient names, diagnoses, or specimen identifiers through that form. Link prospects to a secure operational intake only after qualification. Offer a paid ten-business-day pilot covering one route or one bounded service window, with written rates, acceptance criteria, exception reporting, and exit terms. For example, twenty completed courier runs at $140 produce $2,800 billings, $1,540 driver settlements, and $1,260 retained contribution before dispatch overhead. A proposed 98% on-time target cannot be meaningfully estimated from twenty runs: nineteen timely runs equal 95%, while twenty equal 100%. Report raw counts alongside percentages and investigate every late event. The recurring agreement should follow evidence of executed service, invoice acceptance, and backup performance. Count a win only when a signed recurring assignment exists; a directory listing, verbal referral, or unpaid demonstration is not a won contract.

sections.heading: 4. Close objections, isolate the tax-service adjacency, and protect delivery
paragraphs: Answer objections with narrower operating commitments rather than indiscriminate discounts. When a broker says its network is full, ask whether a specific evening window or accessible-vehicle gap remains uncovered and request the formal supplier process. When a laboratory says the incumbent is cheaper, compare complete pickup windows, exception response, receiving cutoffs, and temperature evidence, not unsupported claims about clinical outcomes. When a hospital requests immediate unlimited coverage, offer a limited geography with a named escalation path and measurable capacity. When a buyer refuses an availability fee, sell scheduled completed work without promising exclusive standby resources. A $95 STAT dispatch with $52.25 driver settlement leaves $42.75 before overhead; an unpriced hour of dedicated standby can erase that contribution. If a prospect demands unpaid work, propose a smaller paid test rather than normalizing free transport. Do not pay per-patient referral bounties to discharge staff or facility employees. Remuneration intended to induce federally reimbursable business raises issues under 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b); any marketing arrangement needs its own factual assessment. A procurement introduction does not justify a hidden commission. Record the objection, revised scope, economic effect, and buyer response before issuing revised terms.

The ninth mapped play is wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine, an adjacent employer service rather than a transportation revenue source. Offer employer-authorized Form 8850 workflow support only after checking 26 U.S.C. 51 authorization for the actual hire date, state workforce agency procedures, and the generally applicable 28-day certification submission deadline. Because the prior authorization covered workers beginning work before January 1, 2026, verify any extension before marketing credits for later hires. Contractor settlements do not become qualifying employee wages. For an illustrative authorized cohort, ten certified employees each meeting the applicable 400-hour requirement and $6,000 eligible wage cap could produce ten times $2,400, or $24,000, before employer-specific limitations; target groups and hours can change those amounts. A hypothetical permitted 10% outcome fee would be $2,400, but professional fee restrictions, including 31 CFR 10.27 where applicable, control the engagement. Separately evaluate Section 41 research activities, business components, uncertainty, experimentation, qualified expenses, and wage coordination; buying dispatch software does not establish research eligibility. Exclude unsupported claims. The fallback is independent tax review and fixed-fee documentation, such as twelve substantiated work hours at $125 for $1,500, without a credit promise or transport referral condition. Keep all such fees outside the canonical transport scenarios.

Close the transport agreement with an evidence package that matches the actual service. Where the relationship creates business-associate duties, execute the required HIPAA agreement under 45 CFR 164.502(e) and 164.504(e); do not assume every courier relationship has identical status or that a narrow conduit exception automatically covers dispatch software storing patient data. Apply minimum-necessary access where required and separate sales records from operational records. For specimens, have the responsible shipper establish classification and packaging; Category B UN3373 requirements under 49 CFR 173.199 are not a universal rule for every medical shipment. Address employee exposure under 29 CFR 1910.1030 where applicable, with training, exposure controls, and incident response. CLIA certification belongs to laboratory operations and does not credential a transport company. Use barcode handoffs, timestamps, receiving confirmation, and specified temperature evidence without claiming that a scan proves specimen integrity. Review owner-operator classification under applicable state law and federal standards; a signed contractor agreement alone settles nothing. After the first three wins, review collections, missed windows, driver concentration, and backup failures every week. Expand only the service patterns whose collected contribution and operational evidence support the next commitment.

sections.heading: 1. Admit only serviceable demand and price the nine operating plays
paragraphs: Begin with a payer contract, a service boundary, and a verifiable operator, not a purchased list of patients. Candidate #34 combines healthcare logistics brokerage with capacity coordination; underlying medical spending and patient benefits never become dispatch revenue. Create separate intake queues for authorized passenger trips and laboratory consignments because eligibility, equipment, evidence, and escalation differ. A passenger record needs the payer authorization reference, permitted transport mode, pickup window, destination, mobility requirements, and return arrangement. A specimen record needs the ordering facility, packaging classification, required temperature range, receiving laboratory cutoff, and custody identifiers. Keep clinical descriptions outside the commercial ledger. RouteGenie or MediRoutes can supply scheduling and GPS evidence, but confirm contractual export rights and actual integration support before promising automation. Dispatch accepts work only after checking the specific driver's credential dates, vehicle suitability, insurance scope, and available service interval. A wheelchair booking cannot silently become a sedan booking because the cheaper vehicle is nearby. When capacity fails, contact the contracted broker or laboratory immediately and document the authorized substitute or cancellation. Never send an unqualified replacement to preserve an attractive spread; the apparent contribution disappears when the service is rejected.

The required acquisition mapping is google_maps_gbp_lead_gen_network. Apply it to genuine local transport businesses rather than copying a trades directory into healthcare. A partner must actually operate the represented business, control its eligible location, and satisfy Google's current verification and representation rules. Never publish nine profiles for nine rented mailing addresses. At an illustrative $600 monthly acquisition cost, twenty qualified facility inquiries cost $30 each; five converted accounts cost $120 each. If those accounts generate forty authorized $80 legs monthly, gross billings are $3,200 and retained contribution is $1,440 before overhead. These are channel economics, not additional revenue layered onto the canonical case. Use call tracking without recording patient conversations by default, disclose recording where required, and keep review requests free of treatment details. The fallback is one legitimate partner location capable of live video verification, paired with useful organic city service pages. A service-area business should follow address-display requirements rather than pretending its yard receives patients. Do not pay healthcare referral sources per reimbursable patient; assess remuneration arrangements against 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b). Route emergency symptoms to emergency services instead of treating every incoming call as a dispatch opportunity.

The remaining eight mapped plays are chapter-level operating applications, not additional externally supplied play identifiers: Medicaid standing orders, workers' compensation transport, discharge coverage, dialysis returns, scheduled specimen routes, STAT specimens, overflow dispatch, and documentation recovery. Price the first three on authorized completed legs, dialysis on separately authorized outbound and return legs, and specimens on contracted route or pickup units. An $80 passenger leg leaves $36 after a $44 driver settlement; a $200 specimen route leaves $90 after $110. A $150 STAT pickup leaves $67.50 after $82.50, but a missed laboratory cutoff can erase the entire invoice. Do not assume a scheduled route's margin survives an unpriced STAT detour. Overflow work requires explicit substitution rights and identical evidence standards; documentation recovery fixes missing support for real services rather than creating another service charge. The matrix below gives each play a measurable fallback. Treat repeated authorization failures as a source-quality defect, not a dispatcher productivity problem. Measure retained dollars per occupied driver hour, empty miles per completed leg, and evidence-complete percentage together. A busy dashboard can conceal unprofitable capacity if deadhead mileage, wait time, and canceled returns remain outside the quoted unit.

sections.heading: 2. Install the six-module ledger and make every mutation replay-safe
paragraphs: Use the six reference modules below as a narrow monetary control plane, not a replacement for credentialing, clinical systems, or a complete claims platform. Save each artifact under its named filename in one directory, initialize SQLite with schema.sql and views.sql, then import the Python functions from the dispatch integration. Python's sqlite3 module provides the database interface without additional packages. Store amounts as integer cents and treat payer plus service reference as the immutable intake identity. A changed quote under the same identity is rejected rather than silently overwriting previously authorized work. Every write acquires BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading mutable balances, so concurrent writers serialize within this single database. A bounded busy timeout can produce a retryable lock error; it cannot produce a half-posted transaction. Keep the database on supported local storage, enable foreign keys on every connection, and restrict direct write access to these functions. Database permissions, encrypted storage, backups, and restore drills remain deployment responsibilities. The reference deliberately excludes patient names and addresses. Its identifiers point to access-controlled evidence in the operational system, reducing the information exposed through billing exports and support logs.

The state machine admits INTAKE or HOLD records into VERIFIED only when a reviewer supplies authorization, service, and custody-or-arrival references; it then recognizes the receivable and creates one driver payment instruction in the same transaction. Presence checks establish machine-readable completeness, not truth: an authorized reviewer must inspect the referenced evidence before calling release. The instruction's stable payout key crosses the payment boundary unchanged. An external bank adapter must support durable idempotency and status lookup before automated submission is enabled. If it does not, use controlled manual release and reconcile the bank reference before any retry; never claim that a SQLite transaction can make an unrelated bank transfer atomic. This design removes read-modify-write races inside the reference database and makes settled-payment recording replay-safe. It does not promise failure-free third-party services. A HOLD is an internal verification reserve, not a representation that customer money sits in regulated escrow. Driver payment terms still govern actual due dates. After recognition, corrections require separately designed reversal entries and supporting review; the supplied functions reject attempts to repurpose a released job or overwrite its evidence.

Recognition follows the supplied agent-style retained-share presentation: a $100 completed service debits receivables $100, credits driver payable $55, and credits retained revenue $45. Collecting the invoice moves $100 from receivables to cash without producing new revenue. Settling the driver reduces cash and the liability by $55 without charging that amount again against retained revenue. Actual principal-versus-agent presentation depends on the executed contracts and control of the promised service; the 45% convention here is the scorecard's explicit modeling basis. The reconciliation view reports gross recognized billings separately from retained revenue, expenses, bank cash, and outstanding liabilities. Bank references are unique across cash events, so a reused transaction reference cannot settle two jobs accidentally. Partial customer receipts are supported, while driver settlement is intentionally one complete payment per instruction. Split settlements require a distinct installment design before use. The QA module checks integrity, foreign keys, balanced entries, revenue allocation, instruction settlement, and the balance-sheet identity. Reconcile its cash output to an independent bank statement daily. The code is a reference artifact supplied for implementation; execution, load testing, and integration verification have not been performed here.

from __future__ import annotations
import json
import os
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager

def canonical(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))

@contextmanager
def tx():
    db = sqlite3.connect(os.environ.get("FYMC_DB", "dispatch.db"),
                         timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
    try:
        db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        yield db
        db.commit()
    except BaseException:
        db.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        db.close()

def post(db, key, job_id, kind, payload, lines):
    if not key or sum(lines.values()) != 0:
        raise ValueError("A keyed, balanced event is required")
    encoded = canonical(payload)
    old = db.execute(
        "SELECT job_id,kind,payload FROM events WHERE event_key=?",
        (key,)
    ).fetchone()
    if old is not None:
        if tuple(old) != (job_id, kind, encoded):
            raise ValueError("Event identity reused with different content")
        return False
    db.execute("INSERT INTO events(event_key,job_id,kind,payload) VALUES(?,?,?,?)",
               (key, job_id, kind, encoded))
    db.executemany("INSERT INTO entries VALUES(?,?,?)",
                   [(key, account, cents) for account, cents in lines.items()
                    if cents])
    return True

def intake(payer, service_ref, lane, gross, driver):
    if not payer or not service_ref or lane not in ("NEMT", "ROUTE", "STAT"):
        raise ValueError("Valid payer, service identity, and lane required")
    if type(gross) is not int or type(driver) is not int:
        raise ValueError("Amounts must be integer cents")
    if not 0 < driver < gross:
        raise ValueError("Positive driver share must be below gross")
    retained = gross - driver
    score = 100 if lane == "STAT" else 50
    expected = (lane, gross, driver, retained, score)
    with tx() as db:
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE payer=? AND service_ref=?",
            (payer, service_ref)
        ).fetchone()
        if row is not None:
            actual = tuple(row[k] for k in
                           ("lane", "gross", "driver", "retained", "score"))
            if actual != expected:
                raise ValueError("Intake replay conflicts with stored quote")
            return row["id"]
        cursor = db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO jobs(payer,service_ref,lane,gross,driver,retained,score) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (payer, service_ref) + expected
        )
        return cursor.lastrowid
Identical intake retries return one job; conflicting quotes fail without altering prior records

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS ledger_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='AR' AND v.kind='recognize'
                      THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS gross_billings_cents,
    -COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='RETAINED_REVENUE'
                       THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS retained_revenue_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='OPEX'
                      THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS operating_cost_cents,
    -COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account IN ('RETAINED_REVENUE','OPEX')
                       THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS owner_profit_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='AR'
                      THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS receivables_cents,
    -COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='DRIVER_PAYABLE'
                       THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS driver_payable_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='CASH'
                      THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS cash_cents,
    -COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.account='CAPITAL'
                       THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END),0) AS capital_cents
FROM entries e JOIN events v ON v.event_key=e.event_key;
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS ready_driver_payments AS
SELECT payout_key,job_id,cents
FROM payout_outbox WHERE status='READY';
Independent aggregates avoid join multiplication; positive liabilities remain distinct from recognized retained revenue

from __future__ import annotations
from core import tx

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(message)

def run():
    with tx() as db:
        require(db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok",
                "Database integrity check failed")
        require(not db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall(),
                "Foreign key check failed")
        bad = db.execute(
            "SELECT v.event_key FROM events v LEFT JOIN entries e "
            "ON e.event_key=v.event_key GROUP BY v.event_key "
            "HAVING COUNT(e.account)<2 OR SUM(e.cents)!=0"
        ).fetchall()
        require(not bad, "Unbalanced or incomplete event")
        for job in db.execute("SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE status='RECOGNIZED'"):
            lines = dict(db.execute(
                "SELECT account,cents FROM entries WHERE event_key=?",
                ("recognize:" + str(job["id"]),)
            ).fetchall())
            require(lines == {
                "AR": job["gross"],
                "DRIVER_PAYABLE": -job["driver"],
                "RETAINED_REVENUE": -job["retained"]
            }, "Recognition allocation mismatch")
            instruction = db.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM payout_outbox WHERE job_id=?", (job["id"],)
            ).fetchone()
            require(instruction is not None, "Driver instruction missing")
            require(instruction["cents"] == job["driver"],
                    "Driver instruction amount mismatch")
            paid = db.execute(
                "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(e.cents),0) FROM entries e "
                "JOIN events v ON v.event_key=e.event_key "
                "WHERE v.job_id=? AND v.kind='payout' "
                "AND e.account='DRIVER_PAYABLE'", (job["id"],)
            ).fetchone()[0]
            expected = job["driver"] if instruction["status"] == "SETTLED" else 0
            require(paid == expected, "Driver settlement state mismatch")
            if instruction["status"] == "SETTLED":
                require(db.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM bank_refs WHERE bank_ref=?",
                    (instruction["bank_ref"],)
                ).fetchone() is not None, "Settlement bank reference missing")
        missing = db.execute(
            "SELECT v.event_key FROM events v LEFT JOIN bank_refs b "
            "ON b.event_key=v.event_key "
            "WHERE v.kind IN ('collection','payout','expense','capital') "
            "AND b.event_key IS NULL"
        ).fetchall()
        require(not missing, "Cash event lacks bank reference")
        snapshot = dict(db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM ledger_reconciliation"
        ).fetchone())
        require(
            snapshot["cash_cents"] + snapshot["receivables_cents"]
            - snapshot["driver_payable_cents"]
            == snapshot["capital_cents"] + snapshot["owner_profit_cents"],
            "Balance-sheet identity failed"
        )
        print(snapshot)

sections.heading: 3. Run evidence-first dispatch, claims scrubbing, and exception recovery
paragraphs: At shift opening, compare today's standing orders against payer eligibility, authorization limits, driver availability, and facility calendars. A recurring dialysis schedule is not perpetual authority to invoice every planned leg. Confirm cancellations and hospital admissions before creating driver commitments. The dispatcher owns timing and exception routing; the second full-time role owns credential files, evidence review, invoicing, and receivables. Contractors supply service capacity under arrangements assessed against actual state labor rules, not merely documents titled independent contractor agreements. The scorecard's two contractors represent modeled contractor relationships or capacity equivalents, not proof that two individual drivers can fulfill every illustrative service unit. Validate occupied hours, subcontract rights, and backup coverage against the selected route mix. For each completed passenger leg, capture scheduled and actual times, vehicle and operator identifiers, authorized mode, distance basis, and required rider or facility acknowledgment. For each specimen handoff, capture container identifier, sender, recipient, time, seal condition, and temperature evidence when required. GPS establishes location corroboration; it does not independently prove patient boarding, specimen integrity, or successful delivery. Close these gaps before the shift ends, while the responsible people can still resolve conflicting records.

Separate claim creation from evidence approval. Where the payer actually requires an 837P transaction, map the contracted transport code, modifiers, units, service dates, provider identifiers, and authorization into its companion-guide requirements. Other brokers require portal uploads, trip files, or ordinary invoices; forcing every account through professional claims EDI creates avoidable rejects. Preserve transmission identifiers and the payer's acknowledgments. A 999 or 277CA response can establish transaction or claim acceptance status without establishing payment; reconcile later remittance and bank receipt separately. Scrub duplicate service references, expired authorizations, incompatible transport modes, unsupported mileage, and missing signatures before submission. Hold rejected records in an exception queue with an owner and next action, not a spreadsheet copied between departments. A corrected resubmission must retain its relationship to the original service and claim version. Never recognize the same leg again because its payer control number changed. Review aging by service cohort, submission date, and contractual due date so documentation delay does not masquerade as ordinary broker float. When a payer disputes a real service, preserve the original evidence and pursue the contract's correction or appeal process rather than editing history.

Specimen safety starts with classification by the responsible shipper, not with a dispatcher applying a universal UN3373 sticker. Category B infectious substances require the applicable packaging and marking provisions of 49 CFR 173.199; Category A material and other dangerous goods require different handling. Qualified staff must identify exempt specimens correctly rather than treating exemption as a sales shortcut. The laboratory's 42 CFR 493.1242 specimen procedures define collection, transport, preservation, and acceptability expectations that should become contract fields and pickup checks. Where employees face occupational exposure, 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires the relevant exposure-control measures, training, and protective practices. Assign packaging responsibility explicitly and decline damaged or improperly prepared consignments until the shipper resolves them. For protected health information, determine each party's actual HIPAA role, execute required business associate agreements, and apply minimum-necessary access. The narrow conduit treatment is fact-specific and should not be assumed for a dispatch operation storing identifiable trip histories. Keep clinical messages out of general messaging channels. A lost package, temperature excursion, misdirected patient record, or missed STAT cutoff needs an immediate named escalation path and preserved timestamps, not a retrospective note after invoicing.

sections.heading: 4. Walk three service cohorts from demand screening to reconciled cash
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk starts after contracting and credentialing, not on the day the founder first begins prospecting. The stated two-to-five month first-deal interval remains separate from this production window. Each month begins with 1,020 candidate service units at an illustrative $77,083.33 aggregate accepted billing target. Twenty candidates fail eligibility or capacity checks before commitment, leaving 1,000 completed billable units. The third month's aggregate is $77,083.34 to allocate the quarter's final cent correctly. A service unit can be a passenger leg or a contracted specimen route; it is not necessarily a unique patient or new customer. The blended price is a planning device, not a quoted universal rate. Thirty completed units per month initially fail documentation scrubs and are corrected before the contractual invoice cutoff. Therefore permanent recognized losses are zero in this clean Base bridge, while pre-service screening losses remain visible. Any uncorrected services, refund liability, or payer reduction would require an explicit adverse-case adjustment instead of being hidden inside collections. Keep acquisition inquiries, authorized service orders, performed units, and recognized invoices as four separate counts in the operating dashboard.

Assume each month's recognized invoices are deposited during the following month, approximating a clean Net-30 cycle after timely submission. Driver settlements and operating deductions are paid during the service month, with no opening receivable or driver liability. This assumption isolates the working-capital effect; Net-45, delayed batch acceptance, or unpaid scrubs would push cash later. Monthly retained revenue is $34,687.50. Driver settlements are $42,395.83, $42,395.83, and $42,395.84, preserving the quarter's exact 55% aggregate. Monthly operating deductions total $20,812.50: an explicit illustrative split assigns $18,000 to recurring run costs and $2,812.50 to variable administration and exception handling. The supplied $3,500–$18,000 monthly opex range cannot describe every operating deduction at the Base revenue and profit levels; this bridge uses its upper end for recurring costs and shows the additional variable amount rather than concealing the mismatch. Total annual operating deductions are $249,750. Include paid staffing and founder service compensation, if applicable, inside that total rather than subtracting them again from the stated owner profit. Owner distributions, taxes, borrowing, and equipment purchases are outside this simplified cash walk.

Month 1 consumes $63,208.33 before any collection. Starting with $65,000 of available working cash leaves only $1,791.67 at its close; that opening balance is not evidence that the same amount also funds setup purchases. Month 2 collects $77,083.33 and adds $13,875.00 of cash. Month 3 collects another $77,083.33 and adds $13,874.99 because its driver allocation contains the quarter's extra cent. Ending cash is $29,541.66, with $77,083.34 still receivable. Across ninety days, $231,250 gross billings produce $104,062.50 retained revenue, $62,437.50 operating deductions, and $41,625 owner profit. The reconciliation is exact: $41,625 profit minus $77,083.34 receivable growth equals negative $35,458.34 operating cash flow. Multiply the quarter's service economics by four to obtain $925,000 gross billings, $416,250 retained revenue, and $166,500 annual owner profit. Do not multiply the startup cash deficit by four; mature cohorts collect prior-period invoices. An additional half-month collection delay can tie up roughly $38,542 more receivables at this billing pace. The $15,000 startup floor therefore requires a materially smaller launch, faster payment terms, or separately secured working capital.

sections.heading: 1. Build a dated facility and contracting graph before buying enrichment
paragraphs: Start with organizations, service locations, and contracting entities, not patient records. The desk's nine working applications are standing-order scouting, laboratory lane prospecting, workers' compensation sourcing, credential verification, exclusion screening, dispatch telemetry, claims reconciliation, specimen custody, and rank_and_rent_pay_per_call_routing. These labels organize this chapter's workflow; they are not substitutes for a payer's actual authorization rules. Use the NPPES NPI Registry to identify organizational providers, then join CMS facility datasets and CLIA records to physical locations. Store NPI, CLIA identifier where applicable, organization name, service address, source URL, retrieval time, source publication date, and match confidence. Keep an address history because a mailing address can differ from the pickup entrance. An NPI establishes an enumeration record, not Medicaid enrollment, ownership of a vehicle fleet, or demand for transportation. A CLIA certificate establishes a laboratory's certification attributes, not permission to carry every specimen category. For standing-order scouting, forty verified facilities producing eight qualified conversations and two contracts is a testable funnel, not a forecast. At thirty weekly legs per contract and $40 contracted billings per leg, two contracts represent $124,800 annual billings over fifty-two weeks; apply the actual settlement schedule before calling that opportunity revenue.

Build an enrichment waterfall that stops as soon as the next operating decision becomes supportable. First resolve the legal organization through NPPES and the relevant Secretary of State registry. Second establish facility type through CMS, CLIA, or a state licensing portal. Third confirm service geography and a published business telephone number from the organization's own website. Fourth use SAM.gov, state procurement notices, and public contract awards to identify the buying office and renewal calendar. Finally call the published switchboard to verify the transportation or laboratory logistics contact. Never purchase patient-level demand estimates or append health conditions to business contacts. Twenty laboratory prospects costing twelve minutes each consume four research hours; at an illustrative $30 loaded hourly cost, the batch costs $120 before subscriptions. One verified route opportunity can justify that research, but only after pickup windows and required packaging are confirmed. If a commercial enrichment vendor cannot explain provenance, retain the public switchboard and continue manually. When a portal blocks automated access, use its documented download or request public procurement documents through the agency's records process. Public availability does not establish permission to bypass authentication, scrape restricted pages, or redistribute protected material.

Separate discovery freshness from eligibility freshness. A quarterly facility file can support territory planning while being too old to clear tomorrow's assignment. Preserve both the date a source published its record and the date the desk retrieved it; these answer different questions. Before bidding, verify that the solicitation remains open, amendments are incorporated, and the contracting organization actually buys the service being offered. Before assignment, verify required provider enrollment, driver qualifications, insurance, and exclusions against the applicable program and contract. OIG's LEIE and SAM exclusions serve different purposes, so a clear result in one cannot replace the other. Resolve possible matches with authorized identifiers through the official process rather than rejecting someone on name similarity alone. For workers' compensation sourcing, six employer or administrator conversations yielding one ten-trip weekly lane at $55 per trip would produce $28,600 annual billings; the fallback is a written spot-service arrangement, not invented standing demand. Assign every source an owner and expiration rule. If the newest registry snapshot cannot be downloaded, retain the last verified version for prospecting, mark its age visibly, and suspend decisions that require current verification until the authoritative check succeeds.

sections.heading: 2. Buy interfaces that produce evidence, not dashboards that merely display activity
paragraphs: Move into permissioned systems only after the public-data graph identifies a qualified opportunity. RouteGenie and MediRoutes can support dispatch and vehicle visibility, but do not assume every subscription exposes the same API, webhook, or broker integration. Obtain written interface documentation, field definitions, export rights, retention terms, and the relevant business associate agreement before transmitting protected health information. Ask whether a trip event represents device capture, server receipt, dispatcher entry, or a later correction. Each timestamp supports a different audit claim. Test an authorized sandbox with a created trip, reassignment, late pickup, cancellation, completed leg, and corrected completion. Require durable event identifiers and preserve original events when corrections arrive. For dispatch telemetry, reducing eight daily status calls by three minutes each saves two hours over five operating days; value that at the desk's actual labor cost rather than promising staff elimination. If the vendor interface fails, retain a secure export and documented telephone dispatch procedure with later reconciliation. Do not quietly switch to personal messaging accounts. A resilient small desk needs one tested manual path, one exception owner, and a clear recovery sequence more than it needs a second live map.

Treat claims and payments as a contract-specific exchange, not a universal 837P pipeline. Some NEMT arrangements use professional claims with payer companion guides; others require a broker portal, proprietary trip file, or invoice. Where authorized, an 837P carries claim submissions, a 999 reports implementation acknowledgments, a 277CA reports claim acceptance status, and an 835 explains remittance adjustments and payment allocation. Neither transport-level delivery nor an accepted claim proves payment. Stedi can support documented healthcare transaction workflows, while Availity access and transaction availability depend on the payer connection and product. Keep payer identifiers, control numbers, trip references, adjustment codes, and bank reconciliation evidence linked without copying full patient details into every table. For claims reconciliation, recovering six payable $45 legs from a missing-document queue restores $270 of billings; under the illustrative 45% retained-share convention, that represents $121.50 before additional overhead, not $270 of profit. A corrected submission still needs duplicate detection. When a clearinghouse connection is unavailable, use the payer's permitted portal or secure file route, retain the submission receipt, and reconcile its identifier before the automated connector resumes. Never resubmit blindly because a local request timed out.

Keep routing intelligence separate from medical data. Google Maps Platform Routes API can estimate travel times from coordinates without receiving patient names, diagnoses, or specimen identifiers. Review current product terms before storing results or combining them with other map products. For specimen custody, a Zebra scanner can capture a laboratory-issued barcode into an approved application, but the scanner itself does not establish chain of custody. Record the authorized pickup, handoff, temperature evidence where required, receiving acceptance, and exception resolution. One missed $80 STAT collection can also cause a redraw, contract penalty, or lost account; those consequences need their own evidence rather than an invented multiplier. Classification controls packaging: DOT's Category B provisions in 49 CFR 173.199 do not cover every infectious substance or every specimen shipment. Separate commercial acquisition telemetry as well. Twilio or Ringba may meter inbound business calls, but call metadata and recordings can expose sensitive information. Use nonclinical routing scripts, minimize retained content, and verify the specific vendor services eligible for the required agreement. If navigation or scanning fails, use an approved route sheet and numbered custody record, then reconcile the delayed events without fabricating GPS fixes or original scan times.

sections.heading: 3. Engineer the pipeline around lineage, bounded retries, and auditable exceptions
paragraphs: Implement a narrow pipeline with separate discovery, eligibility, operations, and settlement domains. A small authorized service can use Python's urllib for documented HTTPS endpoints, csv for source exports, sqlite3 for staging, hashlib for content fingerprints, and logging for redacted diagnostics. Those modules do not supply encrypted storage or a complete healthcare security program; deploy them within managed access controls, encrypted storage, backups, and monitored infrastructure appropriate to the records. Keep credentials outside source files and never print authorization headers or patient payloads. Assign internal facility, contract, trip, specimen, and settlement identifiers rather than joining on display names. Preserve raw source snapshots under restricted access, then normalize into versioned records with source lineage. A facility relocation should create a new location version, not silently rewrite historical trip evidence. For credential verification, checking twenty contractors at six minutes each takes two hours; resolving only four changed records can reduce repetitive review, but cannot replace mandated checks. Model valid-from and valid-to dates, reviewer identity, and evidence references. If the authoritative source is unavailable when a required credential expires, prevent assignment under that credential and move the work to an independently verified operator rather than extending the date locally.

Design ingestion as at-least-once delivery with controlled deduplication. For public files, store the source URL, retrieval timestamp, release date, byte count, checksum, and parser version. Reject a supposed CSV download when its content is an HTML login page. For vendor events, deduplicate by vendor account and event identifier, retaining payload hashes to detect conflicting reuse. Where identifiers are absent, agree a composite key with the vendor; timestamp rounding alone can collapse distinct handoffs. Respect Retry-After when supplied, use exponential backoff with jitter for transient failures, and stop retrying authentication or permission failures until configuration is corrected. A payment submission timeout belongs in a reconciliation queue because retrying a non-idempotent operation can create a duplicate. For exclusion screening, a local monthly LEIE index can narrow candidate matches across fifty roster records, but official identity verification remains necessary for plausible matches. Track match status separately from assignment eligibility. Quarantine schema changes rather than shifting columns by position. If a source adds a new identifier field or changes date formatting, preserve the original file and route a small sample to review. Restart from a committed checkpoint only after counts and identifiers reconcile.

Make diagnostics operationally legible: each alert needs an affected contract, a last-good timestamp, an owner, and a concrete next action. Track discovery-file age, credential expirations, unmatched trip events, unacknowledged submissions, unpaid accepted claims, and custody exceptions as separate queues. A green HTTP response cannot clear any of them by itself. Use synthetic records to test daylight-saving transitions, time-zone offsets, repeated barcodes, split outbound and return legs, and assignments crossing midnight. Store timestamps with offsets and retain the original device value; do not overwrite an implausible clock reading with a cleaner invented event. For dispatch evidence, compare GPS sample age against the contract's verification requirement rather than declaring a universal tolerance. For specimen custody, link each handoff to an authorized receiving identity and record temperature requirements supplied by the laboratory. OSHA's bloodborne-pathogens standard applies according to occupational exposure, while DOT packaging requirements depend on shipment classification. For independent owner-operators, contract labels alone do not establish worker status; scheduling, control, equipment, and state-specific tests require operational review. When telemetry is missing, document the exception and seek the contract's permitted alternative evidence instead of backfilling a fictional route.

sections.heading: 4. Price the information edge against retained contribution and cash timing
paragraphs: Keep the scorecard's denominators visible in every dashboard. Conservative gross billings of $250,000 produce $137,500 of driver settlements and $112,500 retained dispatch revenue at 45%; $82,500 of remaining costs leave $30,000 owner profit. Base billings of $925,000 produce $508,750 of settlements and $416,250 retained revenue; $249,750 of remaining costs leave $166,500 profit. Scaled billings of $1,600,000 produce $880,000 of settlements and $720,000 retained revenue; $336,000 of remaining costs leave $384,000 profit. Those profits equal 12%, 18.0%, and 24% of gross billings, or 26.67%, 40.0%, and 53.33% of retained revenue. Under this scorecard's ASC 606 net-presentation convention, retain the $112,500–$720,000 range as recognized dispatch revenue; actual principal-versus-agent conclusions depend on contractual control. Do not label underlying client collections, medical charges, or all driver pass-throughs as operator revenue. Team counts remain 2 FT + 2 C, 2 FT + 2 C, and 3 FT + 3 C. The supplied $3,500–$18,000 monthly operating range is not a replacement for these full annual residual costs; its narrower expense scope must be documented before comparing either figure with a vendor quote.

Treat acquisition tooling as a separate application with its own economics and healthcare boundaries. The mapped TRACK_2 play rank_and_rent_pay_per_call_routing builds local foundation-repair, water-restoration, probate-liquidation, and commercial-roofing hubs, then routes qualifying calls through Ringba or Twilio. Its supplied price band is $75–$300 per inbound call lasting over ninety seconds. At twenty accepted calls and $125 each, gross call fees are $2,500; an illustrative $650 traffic-and-telephony cost and $250 dispute allowance leave $1,600 before labor, overhead, and taxes. This is a separate acquisition example, not an addition to the canonical NEMT scenarios. For a healthcare logistics desk, reuse the routing instrumentation and business inquiry triage, not an automatic per-patient referral fee. Remuneration for federal healthcare program referrals can implicate 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b); a ninety-second call rule does not resolve that issue. Maintain organic city and calculator pages as a traffic fallback independent of a Google Business Profile suspension, while recognizing that organic rankings still fluctuate. Verify Maps listings only with genuine eligible partner locations. Require prepaid auto-refill wallets for the separate commercial buyers and pause routing when a funded balance cannot cover the agreed qualifying-call charge.

Buy tools against measured cash effects, then stress-test settlement timing. An illustrative $600 monthly integration requires $1,333.33 in additional gross billings to recover its fee at a 45% retained share, before incremental overhead; use $1,334 as a rounded planning threshold. Count recoveries only when they would otherwise have been lost, and do not double-count faster collection as additional revenue. At Base annual billings, a steady-state forty-five-day collection interval represents approximately $114,041 of gross receivables using a 365-day year. Forty-five days of driver settlements alone represent approximately $62,723; weekly payouts, denials, payroll, and reserves determine the actual funding need. That illustrates why the supplied $15,000–$65,000 startup range can become tight before the first two-to-five-month deal cycle produces reliable cash. Negotiate settlement terms and stage route growth instead of financing expansion through overdue driver payments. Review tools after thirty days of measured operation: verified prospect cost, prevented duplicate payments, recovered payable trips, custody exceptions, and days to cash. Keep a tool when attributable retained benefit exceeds its subscription, integration, review labor, and failure recovery costs. Retire it when exports and a controlled manual process produce the same evidence more economically.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #34, NEMT & Medical Courier Dispatch Arbitrage, ranks #08 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps nine operating plays across standing orders, workers' compensation, dialysis, discharge, accessible transport, STAT specimens, scheduled specimens, exception recovery, and permissioned outbound infrastructure. The contract must distinguish transportation authority from dispatch coordination, earned fees from disputed trips, and patient information from reusable software. Canonical annual owner profits are $30,000 Conservative, $166,500 Base, and $384,000 Scaled. Those profits follow gross billings of $250,000, $925,000, and $1,600,000, with 45% retained dispatch contribution after driver settlements. Build the licensing matrix, signed buyer terms, custody evidence, payment reserve, and truthful outreach scripts before accepting standing orders.
