sections.heading: 1. Classify the service before accepting the route
paragraphs: Start with a service classification sheet, not a generic transportation agreement. Record the purchasing entity, payer, passenger assistance level, specimen category, vehicle ownership, dispatch role, and every state crossed. Medicaid transportation assurance under 42 CFR 431.53 and transportation provisions under 42 CFR 440.170(a) do not create a universal federal dispatch license. State Medicaid agencies, managed care organizations, and transportation brokers impose enrollment, screening, authorization, inspection, and documentation requirements through their respective programs. Determine whether your company contracts as the enrolled transportation provider, an authorized subcontractor, or an administrative dispatch vendor; those positions produce different billing and credential obligations. Section 1902(a)(87) of the Social Security Act, codified at 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(87), establishes specified Medicaid transportation provider and driver assurances, including exclusion screening and driver licensing requirements. Check the state's implementation rather than treating one broker's credential packet as transferable authority. A wheelchair trip, assisted ambulette trip, stretcher movement, and ambulance service may occupy different licensing categories. Reject an assignment requiring clinical monitoring when the available crew and vehicle provide transportation only. Preserve the written classification, current credentials, and buyer authorization together so dispatch cannot silently expand the service when a facility requests extra assistance.

Build a separate passenger and property authority matrix for interstate work. Federal property brokerage concepts under 49 U.S.C. 13102 do not automatically resolve passenger dispatch status; evaluate the actual arranging activity, compensation, operating authority, and applicable exemptions. Interstate for-hire passenger carriers can face FMCSA registration and insurance requirements even when the appointment itself is medical. California passenger-carrier authority, local vehicle rules, and Medi-Cal enrollment must be assessed independently; California Labor Code sections 2775 and 2776 also make contractor status a separate analysis. New York Medicaid ambulette requirements, transportation manager instructions, and applicable Vehicle and Traffic Law Article 19-A driver rules require another lane-specific review. Workers' compensation transportation follows the relevant state claim authorization and purchasing arrangement rather than automatically inheriting Medicaid rates. Assign one owner to update the matrix whenever a new county, payer, vehicle class, or border crossing appears. Retain official source links, effective dates, and written agency responses where the classification is unclear. The fallback is a properly credentialed carrier with a permitted subcontracting arrangement, or declining that lane; relabeling a carrier as a technology partner does not change the underlying activity. Recheck insurance territories before approving the replacement.

HIPAA status follows the information function, not the word courier. A carrier performing only transient transmission may fit the narrow conduit treatment described by HHS, but a dispatch company storing patient schedules, addresses, appointment details, and trip records will often perform business associate functions. Where that relationship exists, execute the agreement required by 45 CFR 164.502(e) and 164.504(e), including appropriate downstream subcontractor terms. Apply minimum necessary access under 45 CFR 164.502(b), role-based permissions, device controls, incident reporting, and contractually defined retention. Keep patient identifiers out of sales prospecting systems. Specimen transport adds a different classification tree: the shipper must determine whether material is exempt, Category B under 49 CFR 173.199, or subject to Category A requirements. UN3373 is not a universal label for every specimen. Require documented packaging, temperature limits, receiving windows, and a damaged-package escalation process before pickup. OSHA's 29 CFR 1910.1030 applies to covered employers with occupational blood exposure, requiring an exposure control plan and associated protections. CLIA primarily regulates laboratory testing; a courier-only operation does not acquire laboratory testing authority by transporting specimens. Have the laboratory define specimen acceptance criteria and document every rejected handoff.

callout.title: Four checks before the first live assignment
callout.body: A service order becomes dispatchable only when all four records match the actual lane, buyer, vehicle, and information flow.
items: Verify provider enrollment, permitted subcontracting, vehicle class, driver credentials, and interstate authority where applicable against current primary records.
Match the signed service schedule to payer authorization, assistance limits, pickup windows, accessorial rates, and the named escalation contact.

For specimens, obtain shipper classification, packaging instructions, temperature limits, receiving hours, and a named laboratory rejection contact.

sections.heading: 2. Make fee triggers, liability, and retained economics auditable
paragraphs: Use a master services agreement plus lane schedules, not one price sheet covering every passenger and specimen movement. Define scope by geography, operating hours, assistance level, authorized vehicle, specimen class, and excluded activities. A fee trigger should require the buyer's authorization identifier, the agreed service event, and an enumerated evidence packet. State whether a completed trip, documented attempted pickup, approved waiting time, or canceled standing order earns payment; a driver's arrival alone must not become a completed Medicaid claim. Specify invoice delivery, dispute deadlines, undisputed payment timing, correction rights, and access to audit records. For a $100 completed service, the illustrative settlement is $55 to the driver and $45 retained before overhead. A $20 waiting charge earns nothing unless the contract and payer rules authorize that charge and the actual wait is documented. Separate commercial service credits from payer recoveries, and allocate recoveries according to the party's documented error rather than automatically charging every denial to the driver. Where the buyer requires 837P transactions, confirm its companion guide and enrollment pathway; other buyers use portals or invoices. Never promise that a scrubbed claim will be paid simply because it passes format validation.

Preserve the scorecard's distinction between gross contracted billings and retained dispatch contribution. Conservative billings of $250,000 produce $137,500 driver settlements and $112,500 retained contribution; subtracting $82,500 of remaining modeled costs leaves $30,000 owner profit. Base billings of $925,000 produce $508,750 settlements and $416,250 retained contribution; $249,750 remaining costs leave $166,500. Scaled billings of $1,600,000 produce $880,000 settlements and $720,000 retained contribution; $336,000 remaining costs leave $384,000. Profit divided by gross billings is respectively 12%, 18.0%, and 24%; profit divided by retained contribution is 26.67%, 40.0%, and 53.33%. Apply the supplied 45% retained-share convention in the operating model, while documenting the actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent conclusion from control of the promised service. Gross billings are not automatically recognized dispatch revenue. The stated $3,500–$18,000 monthly opex range is not a substitute for the complete annual cost bridge: Base remaining costs average $20,812.50 monthly. Resolve that scope difference explicitly in budgeting. At Base volume, 45 days of driver settlements alone consume approximately $62,723 using a 365-day year, before other cash outflows. A $65,000 startup budget therefore leaves little collection delay capacity without deposits, staged growth, or committed funding.

Negotiate risk allocation around controllable events. A liability cap can reference twelve months of fees, but specify separate treatment for bodily injury, confidentiality breaches, willful misconduct, and other liabilities that the parties cannot or will not cap. Match insurance to passenger transport, hired and nonowned vehicles where applicable, cargo or specimen loss, cyber events, and employer exposures; an insurance certificate alone does not establish every coverage term. Make indemnities fault-linked, state the defense process, and prohibit unilateral settlement that creates new obligations for the other party. A narrow anti-circumvention clause can protect documented commercial introductions for a defined period, but must not restrict patient choice, interfere with payer networks, or become a disguised referral payment. Address the federal Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b), when remuneration could induce federally reimbursed business; do not pay discharge personnel for referrals. Define escalation, mediation or arbitration, venue, governing law, and emergency remedies. Reserve preexisting software and routing methods to their owner while granting necessary service rights. Allocate record custody, access, export, retention, and deletion duties without claiming ownership extinguishes patient rights or statutory access. Require an orderly transition when either party terminates the agreement.

sections.heading: 3. Convert driver and specimen requirements into dispatch evidence
paragraphs: An owner-operator agreement is evidence of intent, not a substitute for worker classification. Federal wage-hour analysis, federal employment tax rules, state unemployment and workers' compensation laws, and state wage statutes can apply different tests. Document actual investment, business independence, opportunity for profit or loss, scheduling practices, vehicle ownership, and the relationship's permanence. California's business-to-business provision has conditions; an LLC, invoice, or signed contractor declaration does not establish the exception by itself. Avoid drafting terms that promise independent businesses while operating exclusive, continuously supervised shifts with no meaningful discretion. Required safety standards, payer credentials, and trip verification remain necessary, but assess how the complete operating relationship functions. Where the model requires employee control, budget payroll taxes, overtime exposure, workers' compensation, and supervision instead of disguising wages as settlements. The scorecard's 2 FT + 2 C and 3 FT + 3 C describe the modeled operating team, not the total available driver network or a classification ruling. Keep each carrier's business records, applicable coverage, vehicle inspection, credential expiration, and signed service terms current. If a carrier loses coverage, remove that carrier from assignment availability rather than relying on a promise to renew after completing today's routes.

Configure RouteGenie or MediRoutes around the evidence the buyer actually requires, and verify the purchased product configuration before promising features. Capture assignment acceptance, arrival, passenger boarding or package receipt, departure, delivery, and exceptions as distinct events. GPS proximity supports a trip record but cannot establish that a passenger boarded or a specimen reached an authorized recipient. Pair location evidence with permitted signatures, recipient identifiers, or barcode scans, and preserve corrections with actor, reason, and timestamp. Use service identifiers rather than diagnoses on driver screens wherever possible. For recurring dialysis transport, confirm each service date remains authorized; a standing schedule is not proof that every trip occurred. For specimens, associate the laboratory accession or approved transport identifier with package count, seal condition, temperature evidence when required, and receiving acknowledgment. Do not photograph exposed labels into ordinary messaging applications. Separate damaged packaging, missed pickup, passenger absence, recipient closure, and temperature excursion codes because their remedies differ. A missed STAT pickup needs immediate buyer notification and a clinical decision by the responsible laboratory or care team, not a dispatcher guessing whether the specimen remains usable. Never backfill a pickup timestamp to preserve the service metric.

Design recovery procedures before selling redundancy. Maintain a lane-specific backup roster whose carriers already satisfy the buyer's subcontracting, vehicle, insurance, and information requirements. An uncredentialed vehicle nearby is not usable backup. For an illustrative $200 specimen route, a $110 driver settlement leaves $90 before overhead; if a permitted recovery costs another $60 without a buyer-approved surcharge, retained contribution falls to $30. Repeated recovery costs can therefore erase the modeled 45% retention even while gross billings remain unchanged. Record recovery expense against the original service and review the responsible failure mode weekly. For passenger distress, drivers follow the emergency response procedure and contact emergency services when appropriate; dispatch must not improvise medical triage. For spills or suspected exposure, isolate the hazard within training limits and activate the employer and shipper response instructions. Billing review should reconcile completed events, authorized units, driver settlements, buyer remittances, and denial reasons before releasing final profitability reports. Preserve records for the longest applicable contractual or statutory period, using separate schedules for trip records, required HIPAA documentation, employment records, and specimen logs. HIPAA's six-year documentation rule does not create one universal retention period for every operational record.

callout.title: Protect the evidence before protecting the margin
callout.body: Experienced dispatch operators prevent small documentation shortcuts from becoming repeated payer recoveries or unusable specimens.
items: Test one complete buyer evidence packet before onboarding a whole recurring route; verify its portal, signature rules, and remittance reference fields.

Review retained dollars after recovery expense by lane each week; a busy route with repeated rescues can destroy the 45% retained-share assumption.

sections.heading: 4. Use truthful buyer scripts and permissioned outbound capacity
paragraphs: The nine mapped plays here are the specified multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters infrastructure play plus eight chapter-local service applications: Medicaid standing orders, workers' compensation appointments, recurring dialysis, hospital discharge, accessible passenger transport, STAT laboratory pickups, scheduled specimen routes, and exception recovery. The service applications are operating examples, not additional supplied catalog identifiers. Prospect purchasing teams, broker network managers, laboratory operations directors, and discharge logistics managers through legitimate business contact channels. Do not purchase patient lists or place diagnoses in outreach. Use this opening verbatim: 'Hello, I coordinate credentialed transportation coverage in [service area]. We are evaluating [specific lane] and can share our verification workflow, documented pickup evidence, and exception escalation process. Who owns vendor qualification for that service?' Replace both bracketed fields with verified facts before sending. For discovery, ask: 'Which entity authorizes each assignment, which credentials must the performing carrier hold, and what evidence releases payment?' Then ask: 'What happens when the passenger is absent, the receiving laboratory is closed, or the approved driver cancels?' These questions expose authorization and recovery risk before rate negotiation. Never describe pending enrollment as approved network status, and never promise clinical capability merely because a driver has healthcare customers.

For multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters, separate the arithmetic from permitted service use. Three hundred inboxes sending 15–25 messages each over 20 business days yield 90,000–150,000 monthly messages; 150,000 is the upper endpoint, not a minimum or an inbox-placement prediction. Thirty sending days yield 135,000–225,000, but volume alone establishes neither buyer relevance nor provider permission. At hypothetical retail prices of $6–$12 per seat, 300 seats cost $1,800–$3,600 monthly before other services. Use Microsoft 365 developer or partner benefits only when their current terms expressly permit the intended production activity; eligibility does not establish unrestricted commercial sending rights. Cloudflare Email Routing is inbound forwarding, not a substitute for an authorized outbound mail service. Use properly licensed SMTP service, authenticated domains, truthful sender identity, and monitored replies. A voluntary limit of two or three domains per tenant may simplify administration but does not authorize otherwise prohibited activity. Remove tracking pixels, validate addresses using permitted services, and recognize that catch-all SMTP responses cannot verify every recipient. Do not rotate domains to evade provider enforcement. The fallback is lower volume, better account selection, and permitted paid capacity, not an instant identity swap.

Apply CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. 7704 to commercial email, including business-to-business campaigns: accurate headers, truthful subjects, required advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out honored within ten business days. Maintain suppression across all sending identities, not just the mailbox receiving the request. Telephone and text outreach requires a separate review under 47 U.S.C. 227, 47 CFR 64.1200, and applicable state requirements; an email address does not establish consent for automated marketing calls or texts. Use this laboratory discovery script: 'Which specimen classes do you release, who packages them, what temperature limits apply, and who decides acceptance after a delayed handoff?' For commercial terms say: 'Our quote separates scheduled service, authorized waiting, cancellation, and recovery. Can we review your evidence requirements and payment timetable before selecting a pilot lane?' Close with: 'If this is outside your remit, please direct me to vendor qualification. Reply stop and we will suppress further marketing.' Include the remaining required sender disclosures in the actual message. Start with one measured lane; calculate customer acquisition cost from collected contribution, including onboarding labor, rather than counting replies as profitable contracts.

sections.heading: 1. Map nine plays into one four-person event backbone
paragraphs: Begin with nine explicit operating lanes rather than nine disconnected applications. This chapter maps the volume's transportation, specimen, and brokerage edges into P1 Medicaid standing orders, P2 workers'-comp NEMT, P3 facility discharge coverage, P4 recurring laboratory routes, P5 STAT specimen pickups, P6 owner-operator capacity sourcing, P7 clean billing and collections, P8 account expansion, and P9 referral-led distribution. These labels are implementation handles, not additional revenue cases. Assign the first full-time employee to dispatch, service recovery, and safety escalation; assign the second to account qualification, billing release, and receivables. One contractor maintains integrations and observability; the other supports credential evidence and quality sampling within their actual engagement terms. The four-person management pod is distinct from the contracted driver network whose settlements consume 55% of gross billings. Contractor labels do not resolve worker classification. Document state-specific control, equipment, substitution, and business-independence requirements before adding capacity. The scaled 3 FT + 3 C case adds coverage and integration resilience rather than assuming software can absorb every exception. Publish an ownership roster with a named backup for each lane and an escalation schedule that matches contracted service hours.

Build the backbone around a canonical job record containing tenant, payer or customer, service type, authorization reference, scheduled window, assigned carrier, evidence pointers, and billing state. Store patient identifiers separately behind restricted access; operational queues should carry opaque job identifiers. RouteGenie or MediRoutes remains the dispatch system where adopted. Confirm the customer's licensed integration methods, export fields, and support commitments before promising webhooks; use scheduled authorized exports when push events are unavailable. A Python intake service validates an agreed schema, verifies signatures where supported, and commits the received event before acknowledging delivery. Use a unique constraint on tenant, source, and event identifier to suppress duplicate processing. Keep event time and receipt time separately because mobile devices can reconnect hours later. Prototype queue transitions with sqlite3 transactions and test fixtures; use a managed transactional store when concurrency and availability requirements exceed that prototype. Write outbound intents to an outbox in the same transaction as state changes. urllib.request can deliver supported HTTPS requests, while json, hashlib, hmac, and logging cover parsing, checksums, signature verification, and structured diagnostics without introducing sibling-module dependencies. Rotate secrets through the deployment's secret store.

Define automation as saved repetitive labor after review and recovery, not the share of jobs touched by a model. Time a representative baseline across research, qualification, fulfillment, and acquisition. An illustrative weekly sample contains 1,000 minutes: 180 researching accounts, 220 checking qualification packets, 420 handling fulfillment records, and 180 preparing outreach. A credible 74% result leaves 260 total minutes, including all reviewer work, exception handling, and repairs attributable to that workload. Record separate category results so easy prospect enrichment cannot hide manual dispatch overload. LLMs may classify public account descriptions, draft customer-specific questions, and summarize already validated exceptions. They must not invent authorization numbers, alter custody timestamps, infer a patient's transport needs, or release disputed claims. Treat uploaded documents and inbound messages as untrusted data, never instructions to call tools or reveal other accounts. Enforce an output schema, enumerated action types, bounded field lengths, and explicit evidence references. The application, not model prose, decides which transitions require human review. Reassess the target after a complete billing cycle, including denied claims and delayed specimen exceptions that arrive after the original job appears closed.

callout.title: Design around the records that brokers actually reject
callout.body: The highest-return integrations preserve evidence before they accelerate assignment volume.
items: Store authorization revision identifiers on each standing-order occurrence; a later renewal must not silently validate an earlier uncovered trip.
Keep pickup, drop-off, mobile synchronization, and server receipt timestamps separate so offline GPS uploads do not masquerade as late service.
Record laboratory cutoff calendars by destination and weekday; a route that works Monday can miss a Friday processing window.
Maintain payer-specific denial dictionaries from actual remittance evidence, then prioritize the three rejection causes consuming the most reviewer minutes.

sections.heading: 2. Automate fulfillment evidence without delegating consequential judgment
paragraphs: Model fulfillment as allowed transitions: requested, qualified, offered, accepted, arrived, picked up, delivered, evidence reviewed, and billable. Every transition records its actor, source event, evidence reference, and rule version. A GPS point near a facility supports arrival but does not prove passenger boarding, completed assistance, or specimen transfer. Configure dwell checks and distance tolerances from actual facility entrances, then route ambiguous events for review instead of overwriting coordinates. Distinguish cancelled trips, rider no-shows, failed pickups, and completed services because their payment rules differ. RouteGenie or MediRoutes exports can feed deterministic checks for impossible sequencing, duplicate assignments, overlapping carrier commitments, and missing trip logs. The dispatch lead decides whether evidence supports completion and whether the contract permits a charge. For STAT work, the system must page an accountable responder when acceptance is missing; placing a message in a queue is not carrier acceptance. Use contract-specific response deadlines, a staffed telephone fallback, and prequalified replacement capacity. Medical emergencies belong with the facility's emergency protocol and appropriate emergency services, not an automated substitution of ordinary NEMT capacity. Keep the original event trail intact when corrections are necessary.

For specimen routes, barcode the package or approved transport container and bind it to the laboratory's manifest identifier without exposing patient details on general dispatch screens. Capture each custody transfer with the releasing party, receiving party, timestamp, location, seal condition, and required transport conditions. Preserve offline scans locally with stable event identifiers, then reconcile sequence and device clock differences during synchronization. The laboratory determines specimen acceptability, packaging classification, temperature limits, and excursion disposition under its procedures. Category B infectious substances shipped as UN3373 require the applicable packaging and marking controls in 49 CFR 173.199; not every specimen belongs in that category. Use laboratory-approved packaging instructions and role-specific training rather than asking a model to classify biological risk. Where occupational exposure exists, implement the employer duties in 29 CFR 1910.1030, including exposure controls and training appropriate to the work. Receiving laboratories operating under CLIA establish specimen submission and handling procedures under 42 CFR 493.1242. A missing scan creates an evidence exception, while a broken seal or temperature excursion creates a handling exception requiring laboratory direction. Neither can be resolved by generating a plausible replacement narrative.

Billing automation begins with the actual payer contract, not a universal assumption that every transportation invoice is an 837P claim. Where the payer accepts professional claims, map validated service data into its applicable 837P implementation and companion-guide requirements through an authorized clearinghouse. Other accounts may require broker portals, structured invoices, or contract-specific files. Check authorization coverage, provider identifiers, service dates, units, mileage treatment, required modifiers, and supporting trip evidence using versioned payer rules. A 999 acknowledgment addresses transaction implementation processing, and a 277CA reports claim acknowledgment status; neither establishes payment. Match later adjudication and 835 remittance where available to the original receivable. Have the billing lead release batches, review unsupported fields, and approve corrections that change amounts or service facts. LLMs can summarize rejection text but cannot choose billable codes from incomplete transport notes. Preserve submission identifiers and check status before retrying after a timeout to avoid duplicate claims. Track Net-30/45 receivables from the contractually relevant acceptance date, not merely the first file upload. Escalate unacknowledged submissions separately from acknowledged but unpaid claims so collection effort reaches the correct counterparty.

sections.heading: 3. Build distribution loops from verified capacity and service evidence
paragraphs: Programmatic acquisition should describe verified service coverage, not mass-produce nearly identical city pages. Maintain a public coverage dataset containing service areas, operating hours, supported transport categories, laboratory cutoff compatibility, and commercial contact channels. Exclude patient information and sensitive pickup patterns. Generate pages only where active qualified capacity and an accountable service owner exist. Each page should answer a buyer's operational question: who handles recurring dialysis transportation, which laboratory corridors support scheduled handoffs, or how a facility requests discharge coverage within stated hours. An LLM can draft from approved structured facts, but the account lead checks every capability and response-time statement before publication. Use source-linked public facility directories and permitted government datasets to identify organizations; do not treat a CLIA listing as evidence of purchasing intent or specimen volume. Record source dates, organizational contacts, and fit reasons in the CRM. Qualify opportunities against route density, payer acceptance, required assistance, and collection terms before spending reviewer time on a proposal. A high-traffic page with no executable coverage creates dispatch debt, while a narrow corridor page can generate an account that improves existing route economics.

Outbound operates as a controlled research-to-conversation loop. Python normalizes organization names, removes duplicate locations, checks suppression records, and produces small reviewable account batches. The model drafts a concise message using public operational facts and one relevant service hypothesis, such as consolidating scheduled lab handoffs along an existing corridor. A person verifies the contact source, commercial fit, and offered capacity before sending. Track replies, qualified meetings, accepted proposals, retained contribution, and collection experience by source cohort rather than optimizing opens alone. Commercial email must follow applicable CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate routing information, required identification, a valid postal address, and functional opt-out handling. Apply suppression across every sender and vendor before the next batch. Calls and texts require separate channel analysis under applicable rules, including 47 U.S.C. 227; an email contact does not establish permission for automated texting. Do not automate unsolicited patient outreach or purchase lists of health conditions. Stop sending to a segment when reviewers cannot answer replies promptly, when capacity becomes constrained, or when suppression synchronization fails. These limits protect the operating loop from selling work the pod cannot reliably fulfill.

Create the referral loop from account-level service results rather than patient stories or per-trip rewards. After a stable service period, give the authorized facility contact a concise scorecard showing their own completed jobs, documented exceptions, response performance, and reconciliation status. Ask whether another location with similar operating needs would value an introduction. Make sharing optional and remove patient identifiers; cross-customer benchmarks require aggregation that actually prevents identification. The next qualified account increases compatible corridor density, which can improve carrier utilization and service reliability, producing better evidence for subsequent introductions. Measure that sequence rather than describing every share as viral growth. Federal healthcare-program business implicates the anti-kickback statute at 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b); do not offer remuneration to induce covered referrals. Review any proposed incentive arrangement against its actual facts before launch, and default this loop to uncompensated business introductions. Expansion offers should name available service windows, pricing assumptions, and authorization responsibilities. Feed rejected opportunities back into capacity planning by corridor and service category. Add coverage only when collected contribution and documented demand support it, not because a content campaign temporarily raises inquiry counts.

sections.heading: 4. Price every automated run and rehearse recovery before scaling
paragraphs: Keep the scorecard intact while making automation economics visible. Conservative gross billings of $250,000 less $137,500 driver settlements leave $112,500 retained dispatch contribution; $82,500 of remaining modeled costs leaves $30,000 owner profit. Base gross billings of $925,000 less $508,750 settlements leave $416,250 retained contribution; $249,750 of remaining costs leaves $166,500. Scaled gross billings of $1,600,000 less $880,000 settlements leave $720,000 retained contribution; $336,000 of remaining costs leaves $384,000. The gross-basis net margins are 12%, 18.0%, and 24%; retained-basis margins are 26.67%, 40.0%, and 53.33%. These are the same profits with different denominators, not additive income streams. Preserve the supplied 45% retained share in management reporting and evaluate actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent presentation from the contracts; gross billings must not automatically be labeled recognized operator revenue. The stated $3,500–$18,000 monthly opex range does not independently reconcile every residual annual cost above, so show its scope separately rather than forcing an unsupported reconciliation. Budget software and review labor inside the modeled cost pool, never subtract them twice or present labor minutes saved as extra scorecard profit without an actual expense change.

Instrument unit cost at the workflow-run level. An illustrative low-sensitivity research run consumes $0.004 of compute, $0.006 of model usage, $0.002 of storage and logging, and $0.003 of delivery allocation: $0.015 before review. If 10% of runs need 90 seconds of review at $30 per hour, expected review cost is $0.075 per run, producing $0.09 total. At 20,000 runs monthly, that is $1,800 and 50 reviewer hours. Those assumptions are a sensitivity model, not vendor quotations or a claim that every clinical workflow needs only sampled review. Consequential releases retain required human checks; measure their costs separately. Count retries, failed outputs, redactions, and storage retention in actual costs. Use small models or deterministic templates for bounded classification, caching only non-sensitive source facts with expiry dates. Limit input length and output tokens, and stop a runaway job with a per-run spending ceiling. Compare cost per qualified account, completed evidence packet, and collected invoice rather than averaging all runs together. An inexpensive draft that creates three additional customer calls can cost more than a fully manual message with clear scope.

Recovery capacity is part of the product. Test duplicate webhooks, out-of-order custody scans, expired credentials, model timeouts, missing claim acknowledgments, and a complete dispatch integration outage. Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for transient failures, quarantine persistent failures, and preserve replayable source events. Maintain a restricted offline contact sheet and minimum necessary active-job manifest for staffed telephone dispatch; reconcile manual actions before automated sending resumes. Apply HIPAA safeguards to systems handling electronic protected health information, including access controls, audit controls, and contingency procedures under 45 CFR 164.312 and 164.308. Execute applicable business associate agreements under 45 CFR 164.504(e) before exposing PHI to processing vendors, and verify the actual service configuration rather than relying on a marketing label. Monitor queue age, unaccepted STAT jobs, custody exceptions, claim rejection rates, and receivables aging with named owners. Base monthly driver settlements average about $42,396; a rough 45-day settlement bridge is about $63,594 before other cash costs. Actual timing depends on collections and payment terms. The $15,000–$65,000 startup range therefore requires staged volume and a weekly cash forecast. Scale only after the pod demonstrates recoverable operations and funded settlement obligations.

sections.heading: 1. Assign four real seats before selling nine operating plays
paragraphs: Build the initial pod around two employee seats and two genuine owner-operator contractor seats. FT1 owns dispatch, customer relationships, credential monitoring, incident command, and the weekly capacity plan. FT2 owns authorization matching, invoice preparation, remittance posting, collections, and the service-month close; they also provide trained dispatch relief during scheduled breaks. C1 supplies qualified NEMT vehicle capacity and documented passenger service. C2 supplies qualified medical courier capacity and specimen handoffs. Neither contractor becomes a disguised employee dispatcher merely because the organization chart needs coverage. Define each contracted service by accepted assignments, equipment requirements, delivery evidence, and lawful performance outcomes, while testing the actual relationship against applicable federal and state classification rules. At scale, FT3 becomes the dedicated dispatch and exception coordinator, releasing FT1 to supervise accounts and service quality; C3 supplies a qualified flex route within their actual credentials. These are four and six people respectively, not counts that quietly omit permanent assistants. If the founder fills FT1, identify that fact in payroll and valuation schedules. If outside carrier companies supply additional capacity, disclose their drivers separately and stop describing total delivery manpower as only six people.

Use one nine-play map to prevent the pod from fragmenting into unrelated service lines: Medicaid standing-order rides, recurring dialysis rides, hospital discharge rides, workers' compensation appointment transport, scheduled laboratory sweeps, STAT specimen pickups, interfacility specimen transfers, pharmacy delivery routes, and contracted overflow coverage. This chapter's operational labels organize the nine mapped plays; they do not establish nine separate revenue forecasts. Tag each accepted job with its play, payer, ordering customer, service class, and assigned contractor. Dialysis work can sit inside a Medicaid standing order, so choose one primary play for revenue attribution and retain other characteristics as secondary tags. FT1 owns commercial commitments for every play, while FT2 owns evidence sufficient to collect each commitment. C1 normally carries passenger assignments and C2 specimen assignments; pharmacy and overflow work require specific qualification rather than automatic eligibility. A pharmacy delivery contract does not itself authorize controlled-substance handling. Each play must fit the same dispatch board, evidence store, and billing ledger. Do not advertise continuous STAT coverage when two contractors cannot cover simultaneous jobs and rest periods. Sell defined service windows, explicit acceptance deadlines, and documented alternatives when capacity is unavailable.

Size the next seat from timed work, not the attractiveness of the Scaled case. For four weeks, record assignment handling minutes, authorization exceptions, pickup-window collisions, collection touches, and actual contractor vehicle-hours. An illustrative hiring trigger is six consecutive weeks above 80% of available dispatch minutes, coupled with contracted incremental contribution sufficient to cover the new employee's loaded compensation and operating buffer. Separately require a vehicle-hour capacity model before adding C3: passenger dwell time, wheelchair securement, laboratory receiving windows, and deadhead mileage all consume capacity even when billings appear adequate. RouteGenie or MediRoutes can support scheduling and GPS evidence, but verify the selected product's contracted features before promising integrations. Use a barcode workflow for specimen events that does not expose patient information on public labels. FT2 must be able to retrieve the supporting event history without asking the founder to interpret private messages. Cross-train the two employee seats on essential exceptions, then test a planned founder absence. A dispatcher should know whom to contact, what service may be accepted, and when the customer must receive a refusal rather than an unsupported promise.

callout.title: Make the smallest pod difficult to disrupt
callout.body: Protect scarce dispatch attention by designing repeatable boundaries before accepting additional service complexity.
items: Attach each dialysis standing order to its current authorization dates; flag renewals before recurring trips continue beyond the authorized period.
Obtain each laboratory's receiving cutoff and rejected-package escalation number; a timely arrival at a locked entrance is not a completed handoff.
Reserve flex vehicle-hours explicitly instead of counting the same contractor as simultaneous passenger backup and STAT specimen coverage.
Export a weekly evidence index with service IDs and document locations so a replacement employee can locate records without searching the founder's phone.

sections.heading: 2. Price contractor outcomes and run an exception-first weekly scorecard
paragraphs: Write compensation schedules by service type, with an accepted base trip or route amount, mileage treatment, waiting-time rules, cancellation terms, and documented accessorials. The canonical 55% driver settlement share is an aggregate financial assumption, not a universal trip-level entitlement. A dense laboratory sweep may support a different settlement ratio than a long wheelchair ride; route-mix totals must still reconcile to the modeled retained share. Pay for performed, documented services on the agreed cycle rather than automatically passing a broker's delayed payment to contractors. State exactly how a disputed custody event or missing trip record is investigated, what evidence the contractor may submit, and which deductions the agreement and applicable law permit. A missing signature is not permission to confiscate an entire week's earned settlement. Specify customer-facing outcomes without scripting every movement of a purported independent business. IRS common-law analysis, FLSA employment standards, and state tests can produce different obligations; California Labor Code section 2775 is particularly important where its framework applies. A contract title, business entity, or 1099 form does not settle classification. If the actual role requires employee-like control, budget employment rather than forcing the economics through a contractor label.

Run a thirty-minute Monday scorecard using the previous completed service week, with a separate aging view for unresolved exceptions. Define on-time pickup as arrival within the contractual window divided by eligible completed pickups; show customer-caused exclusions separately instead of removing inconvenient events silently. Set illustrative internal targets of at least 98% on-time pickup, at least 99% complete service evidence, and at least 97% first-pass claim or invoice acceptance, then substitute stricter contractual requirements where necessary. Report counts beside percentages because one miss among ten STAT pickups is materially different from one among a thousand scheduled rides. For STAT work, measure acceptance-to-arrival and arrival-to-handoff against the specific purchased service window, never an invented universal clinical deadline. FT1 assigns every serious exception a named investigator, customer communication deadline, and closure evidence. FT2 reports denial reasons by service cohort, unbilled completed work, and receivables past terms. Review custody breaks immediately rather than waiting for Monday. Contractor scorecards should distinguish facts from allegations, allow corrections, and track recurring patterns. Avoid blending safety-critical exceptions into an average score that rewards volume while concealing a failed handoff.

Maintain two evidence tracks because passenger transportation and specimen transport have different failure modes. For NEMT, match the authorized rider, service date, origin, destination, assistance level, and required trip verification to the payer's current rules. Use 837P only where the payer requires that transaction; many broker relationships settle through portals or contractual invoices instead. For specimens, connect the package barcode to collection handoff, custody transfers, delivery recipient, and packaging or temperature exceptions without treating the courier as the laboratory's clinical decision maker. Under 49 CFR 173.199, Category B infectious substances have specific packaging and marking requirements; not every medical package belongs in that category. OSHA's bloodborne-pathogens standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030, applies to covered occupational exposure and requires an employer exposure-control approach, not merely a signed driver checklist. Where the dispatcher acts as a HIPAA business associate, execute the required agreement and control access to protected information; evaluate any conduit argument against actual storage and service functions. FT1 checks qualification before assignment, while FT2 checks collection evidence before billing. A clean invoice cannot cure an unqualified vehicle, mishandled specimen, or materially inaccurate trip log.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile retained contribution and cap every economic counterparty
paragraphs: Keep the Formula v2.0 bridge visible in every management pack. Conservative gross contracted billings of $250,000 less $137,500 in driver settlements produce $112,500 retained contribution; subtract $82,500 in remaining modeled costs to reach $30,000 owner profit. Base billings of $925,000 less $508,750 produce $416,250 retained contribution; subtract $249,750 to reach $166,500. Scaled billings of $1,600,000 less $880,000 produce $720,000 retained contribution; subtract $336,000 to reach $384,000. Gross-billings profit margins are therefore 12%, 18.0%, and 24%, while retained margins are 26.67%, 40.0%, and 53.33%, rounded as shown. The supplied monthly opex range of $3,500–$18,000 cannot represent every remaining modeled cost in every scenario: those annual residuals average $6,875, $20,812.50, and $28,000 monthly. Reconcile its scope before using it as a total-cost budget. Do not subtract driver settlements twice or describe underlying medical charges as brokerage revenue. For ASC 606 presentation, document whether the operator controls the promised service before transfer. The scorecard uses a 45% retained-share basis, but actual principal-versus-agent presentation depends on contractual facts; a spreadsheet ratio alone does not establish the accounting conclusion.

Close by service month, customer, primary play, and contractor cohort. Accrue earned billings for completed qualifying services, related contractor obligations, payroll, insurance, software, and identifiable credits in the same period. Maintain separate schedules for unbilled completed services, submitted receivables, disputed balances, and cash receipts. Treat denials according to their cause: a contractual price adjustment is different from a valid receivable becoming uncollectible. FT2 should reconcile the dispatch service register to the billing register and general ledger, then reconcile contractor settlement batches to payables and bank movements. QuickBooks Online or Xero can hold the ledger, but avoid placing patient details in accounting memo fields; use restricted service identifiers linked to the authorized evidence system. For a simple Base cash sensitivity, daily average billings are $925,000 divided by 365. Thirty days of evenly distributed unpaid billings imply about $76,027 receivables; forty-five days imply about $114,041. The additional fifteen days absorb approximately $38,014 before considering payment timing elsewhere. This is a receivables illustration, not a complete cash forecast. Model weekly contractor settlements, payroll dates, taxes, customer credits, and available reserves explicitly; initial capital of $15,000–$65,000 does not automatically finance the mature Base collection cycle.

Set a maximum 25% exposure policy for each customer and economic counterparty, measured across trailing-twelve-month gross billings, retained contribution, and outstanding receivables. Aggregate affiliates and contracts sharing a common broker payment source; four facilities routed through one payer can still create one collection dependency. Also track forward contracted run rate so a new award cannot hide behind trailing diversification. At Base, 25% equals $231,250 of annual gross billings and $104,062.50 of annual retained contribution. At Scaled, those limits are $400,000 and $180,000 respectively. Receivables receive their own percentage test rather than borrowing an annual revenue dollar limit. Early launch will often breach the cap because the first customer represents the entire book; label that as an unresolved exception with a time-bound diversification plan, not as compliance with the target. Pause incremental awards to an overweight counterparty when practical and pursue independent payment sources within existing service geography. Avoid superficial diversification through longer routes that destroy contribution. Stress-test loss of the largest account, a forty-five-day payment delay, and one contractor becoming unavailable together. The pod needs enough liquidity and executable capacity to survive the combination, not merely each event in isolation.

sections.heading: 4. Transfer the book, normalize earnings, and choose sale or distributions
paragraphs: Build a buyer-ready operating book before soliciting buyers. Include executed customer agreements, renewal calendars, rate amendments, assignment restrictions, termination rights, payer enrollment requirements, and any required change-of-control notifications or approvals. A relationship with a hospital employee is not an assignable revenue contract, and Medicaid participation may require separate steps that an asset purchase does not bypass. Maintain a credential register, insurance history, incident log, contractor agreements, and dated evidence of how service exceptions were resolved. Put company domains, dispatch subscriptions, barcode workflows, and operating documentation under company administration with recoverable credentials and role-based access. Require written intellectual property assignments for custom scripts, training materials, and other owned deliverables where ownership has not otherwise vested. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a copyright ownership transfer generally requires a signed writing; paying an outside developer alone does not establish ownership. Separate owned materials from licensed vendor software and document license transfer restrictions. Limit early diligence to aggregated operating evidence and appropriately redacted examples. A prospective buyer's interest does not create unrestricted access to patient information. Route any necessary protected-data access through a documented permitted basis, appropriate agreements, and minimum-necessary controls where applicable.

Price earnings only after deciding what the buyer must replace. For an owner-operated small book, use an illustrative negotiating sensitivity of 2.0–3.0 times verified seller's discretionary earnings, or SDE; this is not a claim about observed transaction comparables. If normalized Base SDE actually equals the canonical $166,500 owner profit, that sensitivity produces $333,000–$499,500 before debt, cash, working-capital adjustments, and transaction costs. Do not assume owner profit and SDE are identical without a reconciliation. For a genuinely manager-run operation, examine an illustrative 3.0–5.0 times normalized EBITDA sensitivity rather than applying an SDE multiple to a different earnings definition. As a separate Scaled sensitivity, assume $384,000 is the earnings starting point and an unexpensed owner role requires $110,000 in annual loaded replacement cost. If no other adjustments apply, the resulting $274,000 produces $822,000–$1,370,000 at those multiples. These assumptions do not alter the canonical profit case. If management replacement is already expensed, subtracting it again understates earnings. Reconcile interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, owner compensation, and genuine nonrecurring items explicitly. A buyer will reject unsupported add-backs and discounts that disappear only while the founder works unpaid.

Earn the upper end of a negotiated range through evidence of durability, not a glossy route map. Demonstrate stable service-month collections, counterparty concentration at or below 25%, qualified backup capacity, repeatable dispatch coverage, and customer retention after the founder stops handling routine calls. Explain any adverse cohorts before diligence finds them: retroactive authorization denials, specimen rejection disputes, contractor classification exposure, and expensive renewal terms can all change sustainable earnings. Present debt-like obligations, unresolved clawbacks, and a working-capital target based on the actual collection cycle. In an earnout, define qualifying revenue, contractor cost allocation, customer transfers, reporting access, and dispute resolution so the buyer cannot change the calculation merely by moving accounts. If retaining the business, apply the same discipline to distributions. Release cash only after funding scheduled settlements, payroll, known taxes, reasonable claims reserves, and a stressed collection buffer. Test at least two consecutive weeks of ordinary founder absence before calling the book transferable; include a renewal, a late payer, and a service exception in the observed operating period when feasible. A durable cash cow and a saleable platform require the same core asset: documented earnings that survive another competent person taking the controls.

chapters.pull_quote: A buyer pays for earnings that survive the founder's absence, not routes that survive only the founder's attention.
action_checklist: Assign FT1, FT2, C1, and C2 to named people; document founder labor, contractor classification analysis, and the measured triggers for adding FT3 and C3.
Map all nine operating plays into one service register with a unique job identifier, one primary revenue tag, payer evidence requirements, and actual vehicle-hour capacity.
Publish weekly contractor and employee scorecards showing numerator, denominator, contractual service window, exception owner, and corrective-action deadline.
Close each service month with the exact 45% retained-contribution bridge, accrued settlements, denial cohorts, receivables aging, and a dated cash forecast.
Enforce the 25% customer and common-counterparty exposure policy across gross billings, retained contribution, receivables, and forward awards; document any launch breach explicitly.
Assemble transferable contracts, signed IP assignments, license restrictions, normalized earnings schedules, and a documented founder-absence test before choosing sale or continuing distributions.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #34, NEMT & Medical Courier Dispatch Arbitrage, holds Rank #08 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint sequences nine mapped plays through a two-employee, two-contractor pod without confusing credentialing progress with permission to transport. Days 1–30 establish buyer evidence, qualified capacity, auditable dispatch, and bounded cash exposure; the expected first-deal window remains two to five months. Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner profits are $30,000, $166,500, and $384,000, respectively. Gross contracted billings are distinct from the 45% retained dispatch contribution. Day-30, Day-60, and Day-90 decisions use explicit evidence counts, collection experience, service reliability, and settlement runway. Scale verified lanes, fix bounded defects, and stop unsafe or structurally unfundable work.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Select One Operating Wedge and Price the Cash Exposure
paragraphs: Start with a bounded service territory, one buyer class, and one dispatch window. Candidate #34 supports nine mapped operator plays; this chapter labels them P1 recurring Medicaid NEMT standing orders, P2 scheduled discharge NEMT, P3 workers' compensation appointment transport, P4 recurring laboratory specimen routes, P5 STAT specimen pickups, P6 broker overflow coverage, P7 consolidated rural NEMT routes, P8 after-hours laboratory coverage, and P9 contracted replacement-driver recovery. These are operating lanes within the candidate, not nine businesses to launch simultaneously. P9 means replacing failed contracted transport capacity, never emergency medical response. Select P1 or P4 as the initial wedge only after buyer interviews establish credentialing requirements, route density, and payable evidence. Keep the remaining plays in a scored backlog. Map P2, P3, P6, and P7 to the passenger workflow; map P5 and P8 to the specimen workflow. Both workflows may use P9, but passenger vehicles and specimen packaging are never treated as interchangeable resources. Assign FT1 to buyer development, contracts, and cash; assign FT2 to dispatch, evidence, and collections. C1 supplies qualified operating capacity and C2 supplies independent backup capacity under properly classified arrangements. The four-person pod has no spare overnight desk.

On Day 1, FT1 builds twenty named buyer accounts using state Medicaid transportation directories, broker contracting portals, hospital discharge departments, workers' compensation administrators, and laboratory outreach teams. By Day 3, complete five discovery conversations and capture the actual purchaser, covered geography, settlement terms, cancellation rules, and required transport evidence. A discharge coordinator's interest is not a payer contract. A laboratory's CLIA certificate under 42 CFR Part 493 does not credential your courier or authorize testing. For Medicaid work, verify the state's transportation model and the broker's enrollment instructions before quoting a start date; 42 CFR 431.53 establishes the state transportation assurance, not universal acceptance of a new vendor. For P3, identify the authorizing payer and applicable state workers' compensation transport rules rather than copying Medicaid rates. Record wheelchair capability, passenger assistance boundaries, loading time, specimen temperature requirements, and receiver hours as separate fields. By Day 7, choose a lane only if two buyers confirm a specific recurring need and one supplies a written onboarding checklist. Otherwise continue discovery without software upgrades, vehicle purchases, or an unsupported promise of immediate service. Preserve interview notes without collecting patient identifiers that the sales process does not require.

Build the cash sheet before buying dispatch software. The canonical startup capital range is $15,000–$65,000, monthly core operating expense is $3,500–$18,000, and first-deal timing is two to five months. Set this sprint's unrecovered cash-outflow ceiling at the lesser of $12,000 or 40% of committed startup cash. Thus a $15,000 launch permits only $6,000 of unrecovered outflow during the first thirty days; a $65,000 launch still caps it at $12,000. Include payroll, insurance deposits, software, training, legal review, and driver settlements less collected receipts in that measure. Existing unpaid commitments also consume the ceiling. Do not solve a cash shortfall by treating employee labor as free or delaying agreed contractor payments. Separately reserve sixty days of forecast settlements plus thirty days of other cash expenses before adding live volume. At Base annualized billings, monthly driver settlements equal $42,395.83, so sixty days alone requires approximately $84,791.67 under a thirty-day planning convention. That exceeds the startup capital ceiling before overhead. Base therefore describes a mature run rate, not a funded first-month launch. Negotiate shorter collections, obtain committed working capital, or start with materially smaller route volume.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Credential Capacity and Rehearse the Evidence Chain
paragraphs: Days 8–10 convert the selected wedge into a documented eligibility file. For each owner-operator, obtain the credentials actually required by the state, payer, service class, and contract: operating authority where applicable, license, vehicle inspection, insurance endorsements, background screening, training, and exclusion checks when required. Verify coverage with the producer rather than assuming a certificate proves coverage for every proposed activity. Passenger assistance and wheelchair securement require demonstrated competence when offered; specimen transport requires the packaging and handling competence appropriate to the material. Use the federal economic-realities framework under the Fair Labor Standards Act and applicable state tests when reviewing contractor status. A contract label does not override actual working conditions. California Labor Code section 2775, for example, creates an ABC framework subject to statutory exceptions that require specific analysis. If the planned relationship fails the applicable test, use employment or a properly structured qualified carrier arrangement and reprice the lane. Do not preserve the 55% driver-settlement assumption by ignoring payroll obligations. C1 and C2 must be genuine usable capacity, not names on a spreadsheet, and neither should be assigned simultaneous passenger and specimen commitments that cannot both be met.

Configure RouteGenie or MediRoutes only after checking the selected vendor's current functions, contract, access controls, export options, and handling of protected health information. Execute HIPAA business associate agreements where the relationship requires them under 45 CFR 164.502(e) and 164.504(e); do not assume every courier relationship has identical status. Apply minimum-necessary access under 45 CFR 164.502(b) where applicable. FT2 needs dispatch details, not unrestricted clinical records. Use individual accounts, prompt access removal, device locks, and documented evidence retention based on payer, privacy, and state requirements. GPS verifies location, but location alone does not establish eligible transport or a valid claim. Link authorization, service date, origin, destination, timestamps, qualified vehicle, required signature, and exception reason to one trip identifier. For specimens, link collection identifier, pickup, custody transfers, temperature evidence when required, and receiver acceptance without putting diagnostic details into ordinary text messages. Test records must be synthetic or properly de-identified. A barcode scan demonstrates a recorded event, not specimen integrity by itself. The receiver's acceptance and the ordered handling conditions complete the evidence chain. Export a complete sample packet before relying on any dashboard.

Days 11–14 are rehearsal days unless contracts, credentials, and operating controls already permit live work. Run twenty synthetic events across ordinary service, late arrival, cancellation, unreachable passenger, rejected specimen, and replacement-driver scenarios. For passenger work, rehearse the broker's escalation window and prohibit backfilled signatures or invented timestamps. For specimens, obtain the shipper's classification and packaging instructions; Biological substance, Category B shipments use 49 CFR 173.199 when applicable, while Category A material requires a different transport framework. Never relabel material to fit the available vehicle or training. Determine hazardous-materials employee training duties under 49 CFR 172.704 based on actual functions. OSHA's bloodborne-pathogens rule, 29 CFR 1910.1030, applies to covered employees with occupational exposure and drives exposure controls, training, and response planning. Record who supplies compliant packaging and who rejects a damaged package before pickup. Test C2's backup response without creating unpaid standby expectations that contradict the chosen working relationship. Require twenty complete synthetic evidence packets, zero unresolved critical handling defects, and a timed failure-response drill. Rehearsal success proves workflow readiness only; it does not prove market demand, collection reliability, or permission to carry passengers and specimens.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Run a Capped Pilot and Reconcile Every Dollar
paragraphs: Release a pilot during Days 15–21 only when the four pre-flight checks pass; otherwise perform the same steps as controlled rehearsals and buyer onboarding work. The canonical two-to-five-month first-deal window makes a rehearsal-only first month entirely plausible. Cap an authorized pilot at ten completed service events per day, one active route per available driver, and the smaller of contracted capacity or funded settlement capacity. This is an illustrative starting limit, not a statement that every route can support ten events. Define an event as one contracted one-way passenger leg or one separately billable specimen movement; do not inflate reliability denominators with each barcode scan. Record miles, paid time, waiting, cancellations, invoice value, settlement obligation, and direct exception cost. FT2 reviews every evidence packet before submission, while FT1 compares the service to the purchaser's authorization. For Medicaid claims, use 837P only when the payer or broker actually requires that transaction and the operator is eligible to submit it. Other arrangements use broker portals, trip files, or commercial invoices. An accepted clearinghouse file is not an adjudicated claim, and an adjudicated claim is not collected cash.

Keep the scorecard bridge visible beside the pilot ledger. Conservative annual gross contracted billings are $250,000, driver settlements are $137,500, and the 45% retained contribution is $112,500. Other modeled costs of $82,500 leave $30,000 owner profit: 12% of gross billings and 26.67% of retained contribution. Base gross billings are $925,000, settlements are $508,750, and retained contribution is $416,250. Other modeled costs of $249,750 leave $166,500 owner profit: 18.0% of gross and 40.0% of retained contribution. Scaled gross billings are $1,600,000, settlements are $880,000, and retained contribution is $720,000. Other modeled costs of $336,000 leave $384,000 owner profit: 24% of gross and 53.33% of retained contribution. Conservative and Base use 2 FT + 2 C; Scaled requires 3 FT + 3 C. The stated monthly core expense range does not replace these all-in annual cost totals. Under the scorecard's ASC 606 agency presentation, retained amounts represent operator revenue; actual principal-versus-agent presentation requires contract-specific assessment. Patient healthcare spending, laboratory testing revenue, and insurance claim value are never dispatch revenue. Publish gross billings and retained contribution as separate ledger measures.

Use a $100 payable-event example to expose fragile pricing: the canonical settlement allocation is $55 and retained dispatch contribution is $45 before other costs. At Base economics, allocating $27 of other modeled cost leaves $18 owner profit per $100 of gross billings. That allocation is a portfolio ratio, not proof that a particular rural trip earns $18. An unreimbursed $20 exception would erase that illustrated profit. Track exceptions against their originating lane instead of burying them in general dispatch expense. Count on-time performance against the contractual pickup window, and count STAT performance against the separately agreed priority window. Record customer cancellations separately from operator failures, while retaining both in the operational log. Measure first-pass packet acceptance only for reviewed or acknowledged submissions; pending files cannot enter the numerator. Maintain a daily receivables aging report with submission date, acceptance date, contractual due date, disputes, and receipt date. During the pilot, review every rejected packet within one business day and prohibit automated resubmission without correcting the underlying defect. RouteGenie or MediRoutes can support dispatch discipline, but neither software selection nor an EDI scrubber transfers responsibility for accurate service evidence.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30: Close the Evidence Pack and Apply Day-30/60/90 Decisions
paragraphs: During Days 22–30, consolidate the operating record rather than opening all nine plays. FT1 closes the cash ledger and obtains written next steps from buyers; FT2 closes defects and documents dispatch workload. P1 can expand into P6 only when overflow windows fit existing coverage. P4 can extend into P5 or P8 only with funded, qualified priority or after-hours capacity. P2 requires discharge coordination, P3 requires its own payer authorization, and P7 requires route-level density evidence. P9 remains a bounded recovery capability rather than unlimited standby. Measure scheduled workload as committed service and administrative minutes divided by paid, covered working minutes for each employee, and separately measure accepted workload against each contractor's available capacity. Keep planned utilization at or below 75% before expanding. The remaining 25% absorbs delays, evidence corrections, and backup coordination; it is not free inventory to sell twice. If one employee's routine shift already requires persistent overtime, repair pricing, workflow, or staffing before adding routes. The four-person pod cannot silently become the six-person Scaled case. Record added staff cost and capacity explicitly before using that scenario as a planning target.

Apply the following thresholds as management rules, not observed industry benchmarks. At Day 30, Scale means authorizing the next bounded onboarding or pilot stage, not assuming mature profitability. Require five completed buyer interviews, two confirmed recurring needs, one written onboarding path, two qualified capacity files, twenty complete rehearsal packets, zero unresolved critical defects, and spending within the cash ceiling. Live volume remains prohibited until all pre-flight checks pass. At Day 60, expansion requires at least sixty completed live events across four operating weeks, at least 98% on-time service, at least 98% first-pass acceptance among thirty or more reviewed submissions, zero missed STAT commitments, and at least 45% realized retained contribution before other costs. Require one paid invoice and the settlement reserve before adding volume. At Day 90, require 150 completed events across eight operating weeks, at least sixty reviewed submissions at 98% acceptance, 98% on-time service, zero missed STAT commitments, and two invoices paid by their contractual due dates. Apply the 45% retained-contribution floor again. With insufficient samples or no payment history, label the decision Fix and hold volume; zero complaints does not establish reliability.

Kill applies immediately to an unauthorized movement, an uninsured assignment, fabricated evidence, or a critical unresolved passenger or specimen safety defect: stop the affected activity, preserve records, and follow required reporting and corrective procedures. A missed STAT commitment freezes new STAT bookings until the cause is corrected and ten consecutive timed rehearsals pass. Commercial Kill applies to a lane with negative contribution after driver settlements and attributable direct costs across twenty comparable events, followed by two documented unsuccessful repricing or routing attempts. It also applies when contracted obligations exceed available cash and committed funding in the rolling thirteen-week forecast; honor existing obligations while stopping new unfunded bookings. Fix means one named owner, one measurable defect, and a seven-day correction deadline, without volume growth. At Day 90, Scale additionally requires four consecutive weeks at or above 12% fully loaded owner-profit margin on gross billings, no undisputed receivable more than fifteen days past due, and utilization within the 75% limit. Increase weekly volume by at most 25%, then recheck after two weeks. No contract by Day 90 alone is not failure: continue a funded, documented onboarding path within the expected two-to-five-month deal window.

chapters.pull_quote: Scale the lane whose evidence, cash, and backup capacity survive a bad day, not the lane with the loudest demand.
action_checklist: Map P1–P9 into passenger, specimen, and replacement-capacity workflows; select one buyer-validated launch wedge with a bounded service window.
Assign FT1, FT2, C1, and C2 explicit responsibilities, verify actual worker classification, and document service-specific primary and backup capacity.
